definition_zh: 朝贡体系；以进贡、册封与回赐串成的区域秩序；（引申）以让利换取顺从的安排
definition_en: a regional order in which lesser states present goods and envoys to a dominant power and receive titles and gifts in return
core_image: 使团抬着本地物产沿驿道进京，礼部逐项核对贡单，回赐的绢帛与印玺随后装箱南归
scene: 驿道尽头，使团把本地的马匹与香料抬上台阶，礼部官员逐项核对贡单，回赐的绢帛与印玺随后装箱南归。The tribute system turned a flow of horses and spices into an ordered queue at the capital gate.
sceneCN: 这里「朝贡体系」指以进贡、册封与回赐串成的区域秩序（第 1 个义项：作为制度整体）；句意为朝贡体系把马匹与香料的流动排成京城门前的一条有序队列。

pos.zh: 朝贡体系；朝贡制度（可数，指一套安排；亦作不可数，指该秩序整体）

derivatives.zh: 贡品；致敬之词（拉丁 tributum「所分配之物」转指所纳之物，由缴纳转指所献之物）
支流的；纳贡的 / 藩属国（拉丁 tributarius「纳税的」，由纳贡者转指汇入干流的支流）
藩属国（tributary + state，由纳贡关系转指政治地位）

senses.title: The system as a whole
senses.definition: the whole set of rules, rituals and exchanges that link a dominant power with lesser states
senses.definitionCN: 把主导国与较小国家联结起来的那一整套规则、礼仪与往来
senses.example: Historians treat the tribute system as a single framework rather than a list of separate deals.
senses.exampleCN: 史学家把朝贡体系当作一个整体框架，而不是一桩桩彼此独立的交易。
senses.why: system names an organized whole, so the phrase points to the arrangement rather than to any one payment.
senses.whyCN: system 指一个有组织的整体，因此这个词组指向整套安排，而非某一笔缴纳。

senses.title: Paying tribute
senses.definition: the act of presenting goods and envoys to a superior power at fixed intervals
senses.definitionCN: 按固定周期向地位更高的政权呈上货物与使节的行为
senses.example: Paying tribute bought peace more cheaply than garrisoning the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 与其在边境驻军，进贡换和平更省钱。
senses.why: tribute began as the name of a payment, so the phrase can name the recurring act rather than the whole order.
senses.whyCN: tribute 本是一笔缴纳的名称，因此这个词组也可指反复进行的缴纳行为。

senses.title: The goods delivered
senses.definition: the specific goods carried inward, such as silk, horses, spices or rare metals
senses.definitionCN: 运入的具体货物，如丝绸、马匹、香料或稀有金属
senses.example: The ledger lists tribute from the south as ivory, ebony and live birds.
senses.exampleCN: 账册把南方所纳的贡品记为象牙、乌木与活鸟。
senses.why: the concrete reading is the oldest one: tribute is first a thing handed over before it is a policy.
senses.whyCN: 具体义最古老：贡首先是交出去的东西，然后才成其为一项制度。

senses.title: Ritual submission
senses.definition: the ceremonial acknowledgment of a superior rank, performed through kneeling, titles and dated embassies
senses.definitionCN: 通过跪拜、称号与定期使团对更高地位的仪式性承认
senses.example: Ritual submission mattered more than the market value of the gifts.
senses.exampleCN: 礼仪上的臣服比礼物市价更重要。
senses.why: the order ran on recognition rather than force, so the ceremony itself counted as the substance.
senses.whyCN: 这套秩序靠承认而非武力运转，仪式本身就是实质。

senses.title: Trade inside ritual
senses.definition: commerce carried on under ceremonial forms, with gifts functioning as exchanged goods
senses.definitionCN: 在礼仪形式下进行的商业往来，礼物实际充当交换的商品
senses.example: Much of the trade inside ritual never looked like trade at all.
senses.exampleCN: 以礼为壳的贸易，大半看上去根本不像贸易。
senses.why: since both sides wanted goods, the ritual frame became the accepted channel for exchange.
senses.whyCN: 双方都要货物，礼仪框架便成了被接受的交换渠道。

senses.title: Investiture and return gifts
senses.definition: the titles, seals and goods sent back, which confirmed a ruler's place in the hierarchy
senses.definitionCN: 回送的名号、印玺与货物，确认某位统治者在等级中的位置
senses.example: Investiture and return gifts made the hierarchy visible to every neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 册封与回赐让周边所有邻邦都看得见这套等级。
senses.why: the return leg completed the circuit: a gift back was a receipt of rank.
senses.whyCN: 回程那一段闭合了循环：回赐就是对名分的收据。

senses.title: Costly appeasement, by analogy
senses.titleCN: 引申：以让利换顺从的安排
senses.definition: any arrangement in which a weaker party buys tolerance by handing over value
senses.definitionCN: 较弱一方靠交出利益来换取容忍的任何安排
senses.example: Critics called the subsidy a modern tribute system in plain clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这项补贴称作换了装的现代朝贡体系。
senses.why: the analogy keeps the shape of the old order and drops its rituals, leaving only payment for tolerance.
senses.whyCN: 这一类比保留了旧秩序的形状而剥掉礼仪，只剩为容忍而付费。

senses.title: A model in the archive
senses.titleCN: 作为史学分析框架的概念
senses.definition: an analytic model used by historians to describe a regional order, not a term the participants used
senses.definitionCN: 史学家用来描述某种区域秩序的分析模型，而非当时人自称的说法
senses.example: The model in the archive has been revised to include private sea trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这一分析框架已被修订，以纳入民间海上贸易。
senses.why: the label was coined by later scholars, so it works as a lens that can be tested and rewritten.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签由后来的学者造出，因此它是一面可被检验、也可被改写的透镜。

intro.en: Tribute goes back to Latin tributum 'that which is paid', from tribuere 'to allot, assign'; system comes from Greek systema 'an organized whole'. The compound is a modern scholarly label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tribute 上溯拉丁 tributum「所缴纳之物」，来自 tribuere「分配、拨给」；system 来自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」。整个词组是近代学术标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tribuere meant 'to allot, assign, grant', and tributum was what was assigned or paid over. The money sense is older than the political one.
items.cn: tribuere 意为「分配、拨给、给予」，tributum 即被分配或缴出之物。钱财义比政治义更早。

items.en: Tribuere came from tribus, a division of the Roman people. The deeper origin of tribus is not established; the old explanation that it meant 'a third part' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: tribuere 来自 tribus，即罗马民众的划分单位。tribus 的更深来源未得到证明；旧说认为它本指「三分之一」，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Systema meant 'an organized whole', built from syn- 'together' and histanai 'to set up, stand'. It passed into Latin and then into English as system.
items.cn: systema 意为「有组织的整体」，由 syn-「共同」与 histanai「设立、站立」构成，经拉丁语进入英语为 system。

items.en: The fixed phrase tribute system was taken up in twentieth-century English writing on East Asian diplomacy, where it named a whole order rather than a single payment.
items.cn: tribute system 这一固定说法在 20 世纪论东亚外交的英语著述中被采用，用来指整套秩序而非单笔缴纳。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and scope): no exact first citation is recorded, the phrase is a later analytic label rather than a self-description, and the pre-Latin origin of tribus remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与适用范围）：没有确切的最早书证；这一说法是后出的分析标签，而非当时人的自称；tribus 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one gathers words from the same Latin verb and the same Greek noun; group two gathers near neighbours with overlapping political meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词与希腊名词的词；第二组是政治含义彼此交叠的近义词。

entries.definition: An adjective or noun for a state that pays tribute or a river that feeds a larger one; it names one member, not the whole framework.
entries.definitionCN: 指纳贡之国或汇入干流的支流，形容词或名词；它指其中一个成员，而非整套框架。

entries.definition: The single payment or the praise offered to a person; the compound adds system and so widens the scope to an order.
entries.definitionCN: 指单笔缴纳，或对某人的敬意之词；加上 system 后范围扩大为一套秩序。

entries.definition: Ad- 'to' plus tribuere: to assign a quality or cause to someone, so it shares the root but not the payment sense.
entries.definitionCN: ad-「向」加 tribuere：把某种性质或原因归于某人，词根相同而无缴纳之义。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus tribuere: to allot in pieces to many recipients, which keeps the original sense of assigning.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 tribuere：把份额分给许多人，保留了「分配」的原义。

entries.definition: The relation in which one state controls another's foreign affairs while the lesser one keeps internal rule; it is the legal frame the tribute system dressed in ritual.
entries.definitionCN: 一国控制另一国外交、后者保留内部治理的关系；它是朝贡体系以礼仪包装的那套法理框架。

entries.definition: Leadership by one state through power and consent rather than ceremony; it stresses influence, not gifts and titles.
entries.definitionCN: 一国凭实力与默认取得的领导地位，不靠仪式；强调影响力，而非礼物与封号。

entries.definition: A state bound to a stronger one by oath and military obligation, a European feudal notion that only partly fits the tribute model.
entries.definitionCN: 以效忠誓言与军事义务从属强国之国，属欧洲封建概念，只部分对应朝贡模式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tribuere 'to allot': tribute is what was allotted and then handed over.
normal.cn: tribuere「分配」：tribute 就是被分配、再交出去的那一份。

normal.en: The family runs tribute, tributary, attribute and distribute, all from the same Latin verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tribute、tributary、attribute、distribute，全出同一个拉丁动词。

normal.en: system is syn- 'together' plus histanai 'set up': a whole standing together.
normal.cn: system 是 syn-「共同」加 histanai「设立」：各部分共同立起来的一个整体。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the frame: pay tribute, send a tribute mission, a tributary state.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这套框架：进贡、派遣朝贡使团、藩属国。

normal.en: Chinese names the same order by a phrase meaning presenting at court, which keeps the ceremony in view.
normal.cn: 同一秩序的中文说法是「朝贡」，即到朝廷献物，始终带着仪式的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor where every gift must pass through a gate before it counts as anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长廊，任何礼物都要先过一道门，才算数。

abstract.en: Picture two rulers exchanging boxes that contain the same goods in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两位君主互送箱子，箱中货物朝相反方向流动。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn not with borders but with arrows pointing inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图不画边界，只画一支支向内的箭头。

examples.en: The tribute system kept the frontier quiet for two centuries.
examples.cn: 朝贡体系让边境安定了两个世纪。

examples.en: Envoys were graded by the size of their tribute.
examples.cn: 使节的等级按所纳贡品的多寡排定。

examples.en: Modern aid programmes are sometimes read as a tribute system in reverse.
examples.cn: 现代援助计划有时被读作反向的朝贡体系。

dict_mnemonic.text: tribute（进贡）+ system（体系）＝ 一圈向内送礼、再向外回礼的秩序；记「货往里走，名往外发」。

root: tribute：拉丁 tributum「所缴纳之物」，来自 tribuere「分配、拨给」，再上溯 tribus「民众的划分」，其更深来源不确定；system：希腊 systema「有组织的整体」= syn-「共同」+ histanai「设立」。整个词组为近代学术标签。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one circuit: goods travel inward, rank is acknowledged, titles and gifts travel back, and the whole circuit is finally read as a model that later scholars can revise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条回路展开：货物向内，名分被承认，封号与礼物向外，最后整条回路被读成一个可供后人修订的模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate where goods enter and sealed titles leave, and everyone reads the queue as rank.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门，货物进去、印玺出来，所有人都把这条队列读成等级。

branches.en: THE CIRCUIT AND ONE PAYMENT: the whole arrangement, then the single act that keeps it running.
branches.cn: 整条回路与单笔缴纳：先看整套安排，再看维持它运转的那一次行为。

branches.en: WHAT MOVES: the concrete goods that make the circuit visible.
branches.cn: 什么在流动：让整条回路看得见的具体货物。

branches.en: TWO HALVES OF RECOGNITION: the bow inward and the seal outward are one exchange of rank.
branches.cn: 承认的两半：向内的跪拜与向外的印玺，是同一次名分的交换。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN MARKET: ceremony becomes the accepted channel for trade.
branches.cn: 藏在礼下的市场：仪式成为贸易被接受的通道。

branches.en: FROM PRACTICE TO LENS: first a modern analogy, then an analytic model open to revision.
branches.cn: 从做法到透镜：先是现代类比，再是可被修订的分析模型。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun built on a verb of allotting with a Greek noun meaning an organized whole, so both halves can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中由「分配」动词构成的名词，与希腊语中意为「有组织整体」的名词接在一起，两半都可按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere gives tribute, tributary, attribute and distribute; Greek syn- plus histanai gives system, systematic and systemic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribuere 衍生 tribute、tributary、attribute、distribute；希腊 syn- 加 histanai 衍生 system、systematic、systemic。

items.example: The verb supplies both the gift and the act of giving it.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时给出礼物与送礼的动作。

items.structure: tribuere + -tum (past participle used as a noun)
items.example: Tributum first named a levy, then a gift to a superior.
items.exampleCN: tributum 先指征收之物，后指献给上位者的礼物。

items.example: A tributary stream feeds the main river.
items.exampleCN: 支流汇入干流。

items.meaning: to assign as a quality or cause
items.example: They attribute the delay to the weather.
items.exampleCN: 他们把延误归因于天气。

items.example: Volunteers distribute the supplies.
items.exampleCN: 志愿者分发物资。

items.example: The tax system has three tiers.
items.exampleCN: 税制有三个层级。

items.example: They made a systematic survey of the coast.
items.exampleCN: 他们对海岸做了系统调查。

items.meaning: affecting the whole rather than a part
items.example: The failure was systemic, not local.
items.exampleCN: 这次失灵是整体性的，而非局部的。

latinEntries.structure: systema, systematis (n., third declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 官僚机构；官僚体制；繁文缛节；（任何大型组织的）层级管理层
definition_en: the system of officials and offices that runs public business through ranks, files and fixed rules
core_image: 一排挂着编号的窗口，表格在窗口之间来回传递，每个窗口只负责盖一个章
scene: 办事的人被从一个窗口送到下一个窗口，手里那叠表格始终少一个章。The bureaucracy moved her file through six windows before anyone read it.
sceneCN: 这里 bureaucracy 指按层级与规章运转的行政机构（第 1 个义项：作为机构整体）；句意为这套官僚机构把她的档案过了六个窗口，才有人真正读它。

pos.zh: 官僚机构；官僚体制（可数，指一套机构；不可数，指这种运作方式）
繁文缛节；官僚作风（口语中带贬义）

derivatives.zh: 官僚（bureau + -crat「掌权者」，由机构转指机构中的人）
官僚的；程序繁琐的（bureaucrat + -ic，由人转指其作风）
使官僚化（bureaucrat + -ize，由名词转指使之变成那样的过程）
官僚化（bureaucratize + -ation，由动作转指该过程及其结果）

senses.title: The administrative apparatus
senses.definition: the whole body of offices and officials that carries out public business
senses.definitionCN: 执行公共事务的整套机关与人员
senses.example: The bureaucracy grew faster than the services it delivered.
senses.exampleCN: 这套行政机构的扩张快于它所提供的服务。
senses.why: the -cracy ending names a form of rule, so the word first denotes a governing apparatus rather than one clerk.
senses.whyCN: -cracy 这一后缀指某种统治形式，因此这个词首先指治理机关，而非某一位办事员。

senses.title: Officials as a body
senses.definition: the class or corps of career officials, seen as sharing interests and habits
senses.definitionCN: 职业官员构成的群体，被视为共享利益与习惯
senses.example: The reform was resisted by the bureaucracy itself.
senses.exampleCN: 改革遭到官僚群体本身的抵制。
senses.why: once offices became careers, the people in them could be spoken of as a single body with its own outlook.
senses.whyCN: 一旦职位成为职业，任职者便可被当作一个有自身心态的整体来谈论。

senses.title: Red tape
senses.definition: the forms, stamps and waiting that a procedure imposes before anything can be done
senses.definitionCN: 办事之前必须经历的表格、盖章与等待
senses.example: Bureaucracy delayed the permit by eleven weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 繁文缛节让许可证晚了十一周。
senses.why: the everyday sense is a metonymy: the apparatus is named by the annoyance it produces.
senses.whyCN: 日常义是转喻：用机构造成的麻烦来指称机构本身。

senses.title: Hierarchy in any large body
senses.titleCN: 任何大型组织的层级管理
senses.definition: the managerial layer of a university, hospital or company, with ranks, files and approval chains
senses.definitionCN: 大学、医院或公司中的管理层，带等级、档案与审批链
senses.example: Every large hospital has a bureaucracy of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 每一所大医院都有自己的官僚层。
senses.why: Weber's analysis showed the pattern is not peculiar to states, so the word spread to any large organization.
senses.whyCN: 韦伯的分析表明这种模式并非国家独有，于是这个词扩展到一切大型组织。

senses.title: Rule by files, not by persons
senses.definition: administration in which written rules and records, not personal ties, decide outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 由成文规则与档案、而非私人关系来决定结果的行政方式
senses.example: Rule by files, not by persons, was the point of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 按规章而非人情办事，正是这场改革的要点。
senses.why: the defining feature is impersonality: the same rule must bind the clerk and the petitioner alike.
senses.whyCN: 其要点是非人格化：同一条规则对办事员与申请者一视同仁。

senses.title: Weber's ideal type
senses.definition: a neutral analytic model of administration by hierarchy, written records, trained staff and fixed jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 一种中性的分析模型：层级、文书、受训人员与固定职权范围
senses.example: Weber's ideal type describes bureaucracy without praising it.
senses.exampleCN: 韦伯的理想型只是描述官僚制，并不赞美它。
senses.why: the sociological sense strips the word of insult and turns it into a set of testable features.
senses.whyCN: 社会学义剥去贬义，把它变成一组可检验的特征。

senses.title: Sluggishness blamed on rules
senses.definition: the pejorative reading: delay, evasion and rigidity produced by too many rules
senses.definitionCN: 贬义读法：规则过多造成的拖延、推诿与僵化
senses.example: The licence stalled for months in what officials called bureaucratic inertia.
senses.exampleCN: 官僚惰性这一说法正好描述了这个贬义读法。
senses.why: the same features that make administration predictable also make it slow, so the word carries both judgements.
senses.whyCN: 使行政可预期的那套特征同时也让它迟缓，因此这个词兼带两种评价。

senses.title: Size and cost of the apparatus
senses.titleCN: 机构膨胀带来的规模与成本
senses.definition: the sheer scale of an administrative machine and what it costs to keep running
senses.definitionCN: 行政机器本身的庞大规模，以及维持它运转的开销
senses.example: Auditors measured the bureaucracy by headcount and floor space.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员用人数与办公面积来衡量这套机构。
senses.why: budgets make the apparatus visible as a quantity, and that quantity is what the word names here.
senses.whyCN: 预算把机关显形为一个数量，这里命名的正是那个数量。

intro.en: Bureaucracy is a French coinage of the early nineteenth century: bureau 'desk, office' plus -cratie 'rule', from Greek kratos 'power'. It began as a satirical label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bureaucracy 是 19 世纪初的法语新造词：bureau「书桌、办公室」加 -cratie「统治」，后者来自希腊 kratos「力量」。它最初是讽刺性标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bureau first meant a coarse woollen cloth used to cover writing desks, then the desk itself, then the room and the office.
items.cn: bureau 最初指铺在写字桌上的粗毛布，继而指桌子本身，再指房间与机关。

items.en: Kratos meant 'strength, might', and the -kratia suffix named a form of rule, as in democracy and aristocracy.
items.cn: kratos 意为「力量、强权」，-kratia 后缀表示某种统治形式，如 democracy 与 aristocracy。

items.en: Bureaucratie was coined in French around the 1810s as a mocking term for government carried on by officials rather than by citizens.
items.cn: bureaucratie 于 1810 年代前后在法语中造出，用来讥讽由官员而非公民运转的政府。

items.en: English adopted bureaucracy in the nineteenth century; Mill used it for the corps of officials, a usage that made the word descriptive rather than merely hostile.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪借用该词；密尔用它指官员群体，这一用法使词从纯敌意转为描述性。

items.en: Weber turned bureaucracy into a technical term for administration by hierarchy, written records, trained staff and fixed jurisdiction.
items.cn: 韦伯把官僚制转为术语，指以层级、文书、受训人员与固定职权范围进行的行政。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of burel, the cloth behind bureau, is not established, and the pre-Greek origin of kratos is unsettled, so any older form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：bureau 背后的 burel 那种布料的来源未得到证明；kratos 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the -cracy or bureau stock; group two holds words for administration and its annoyances.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -cracy 或 bureau 词干；第二组是行政及其麻烦的同近义词。

entries.definition: A single official, formed with -crat 'one who holds power'; the longer word names the system, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个官员，由 -crat「掌权者」构成；较长的词指整套制度，而非个人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing procedure-heavy behaviour; it modifies a noun instead of naming the apparatus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述程序繁多的作风；它修饰名词，而不指称机关。

entries.definition: Aristos 'best' plus kratos: rule by a supposed elite. It shares the suffix but not the desk.
entries.definitionCN: aristos「最优者」加 kratos：由所谓精英统治。后缀相同，词根无关。

entries.definition: Autos 'self' plus kratos: rule by one person with unrestricted power, a contrast to rule by offices.
entries.definitionCN: autos「自身」加 kratos：一人不受限制地统治，与由机关统治相对。

entries.definition: The activity of managing an organization, neutral in tone; bureaucracy adds the sense of ranks and procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 管理组织的活动，语气中性；bureaucracy 另带层级与程序之意。

entries.definition: The permanent employees of the state, named by their employment rather than by their procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 国家的常任雇员，按雇佣关系命名，而非按程序命名。

entries.definition: The delays and forms only, with no reference to the offices that produce them.
entries.definitionCN: 只指拖延与表格，不涉及产生它们的机关。

entries.definition: Officials thought of as a class with shared habits, close to the second sense of bureaucracy.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为共享习气的官员阶层，接近 bureaucracy 的第二义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bureau 'desk' + -cracy 'rule': rule carried out from desks.
normal.cn: bureau「书桌」+ -cracy「统治」：从书桌后面实施的统治。

normal.en: The family runs bureaucrat, bureaucratic, bureaucratize, bureaucratization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 bureaucrat、bureaucratic、bureaucratize、bureaucratization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the complaint: cut bureaucracy, layers of bureaucracy, red tape.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出抱怨的语气：精简官僚程序、层层官僚机构、繁文缛节。

normal.en: The same suffix appears in democracy, aristocracy and autocracy, all through Greek kratos.
normal.cn: 同一后缀出现在 democracy、aristocracy、autocracy，都经希腊 kratos。

normal.en: Weber's four marks: hierarchy, written files, trained staff, fixed jurisdiction.
normal.cn: 韦伯的四项标志：层级、文书档案、受训人员、固定职权。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where every step requires a signature before the next step opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每上一级都要先签一个字，下一级才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that works perfectly and produces only paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一台运转完美的机器，产出只有纸。

abstract.en: Picture a queue in which nobody knows who is first, but everyone holds a numbered slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队列，没人知道谁在前，但人人手里都有一张编号纸条。

examples.en: The new agency added a layer of bureaucracy without adding a service.
examples.cn: 新机构加了一层官僚机构，却没增加一项服务。

examples.en: Small firms complain that bureaucracy eats their first month.
examples.cn: 小公司抱怨官僚程序吃掉了它们头一个月。

examples.en: Weber saw bureaucracy as the most efficient form of large-scale administration.
examples.cn: 韦伯认为官僚制是大规模行政中最有效率的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: bureau（办公桌）+ cracy（统治）＝ 靠一张张办公桌和一个个章运转的统治；记「章多、层多、纸多」。

root: 法语 bureaucratie = bureau「书桌、办公室」（源自 burel 粗毛布，其来源不确定）+ -cratie「统治」（希腊 kratos「力量」，希腊语之前的来源属重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object seen from different distances: the whole apparatus, the people inside it, the paper it produces, the same pattern in any large body, its impersonality, its analytic model, its slowness, and its cost.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是对同一对象的远近不同取景：整套机关、其中的群体、它产出的纸、任何大型组织里的同一模式、它的非人格化、它的分析模型、它的迟缓、它的成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor of numbered windows where a file gains one stamp per window and never quite finishes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条挂编号窗口的走廊，档案每过一个窗口多一个章，却始终办不完。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MEN: first the offices, then the career officials who staff them.
branches.cn: 机器与人：先看机关，再看在其中任职的官员。

branches.en: THE SAME FEATURE READ TWICE: forms make work predictable and also make it slow.
branches.cn: 同一特征的两读：表格让工作可预期，也让工作变慢。

branches.en: THE SHAPE TRAVELS: hospitals and firms reproduce the state's pattern.
branches.cn: 形状在迁移：医院与公司复制了国家的模式。

branches.en: NEUTRAL CORE: rule by files, then the model that states it without blame.
branches.cn: 中性内核：先是按档案办事，再是把它不带褒贬地陈述出来的模型。

branches.en: COUNTED: budgets turn the apparatus into headcount and floor space.
branches.cn: 被计数：预算把机关变成人数与面积。

intro.en: Bureaucracy is a French compound whose two parts still work separately in English: bureau for the office, -cracy for a form of rule.
intro.cn: bureaucracy 是法语复合词，两部分在英语中仍各自运作：bureau 指机关，-cracy 指某种统治形式。

latinIntro.en: The second element goes back to Greek kratos through the suffix -kratia; the first element is French and has no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 第二部分经后缀 -kratia 上溯希腊 kratos；第一部分属法语，没有拉丁来源。

items.example: The bureau keeps the land records.
items.exampleCN: 该局保管土地档案。

items.meaning: a form of rule or dominance
items.example: Democracy and autocracy share this suffix.
items.exampleCN: 民主制与专制共享这一后缀。

items.meaning: a member or supporter of a ruling group
items.meaningCN: 某一统治群体的成员或支持者
items.example: A technocrat governs by expertise.
items.exampleCN: 技术官僚凭专业知识治理。

items.example: The bureaucrat stamped the form without reading it.
items.exampleCN: 那位官员没看就盖了章。

items.example: Bureaucratic delays cost the project a season.
items.exampleCN: 官僚拖延让项目耽误了一季。

items.example: They bureaucratized the volunteer network.
items.exampleCN: 他们把志愿网络官僚化了。

items.example: Bureaucratization followed the merger.
items.exampleCN: 合并之后便出现了官僚化。

items.meaning: the inflated style of official writing
items.example: The notice was written in bureaucratese.
items.exampleCN: 这则通知是用公文腔写的。

definition_zh: 官僚机构的；官僚作风的；程序繁琐、层层审批的
definition_en: of or like a bureaucracy, especially in requiring many ranks, forms and approvals
core_image: 一份表格在六个桌面之间旅行，每张桌面都要求补一份附件，却没有人负责最后签字
scene: 为了改一个地址，她先填表、再复印、再等上一级批准，最后被告知还缺一个签名。Getting an address changed proved a bureaucratic ordeal of forms and countersignatures.
sceneCN: 这里 bureaucratic 形容办事要经过大量表格与层层签字（第 2 个义项：程序繁琐）；句意为改一个地址竟成了充满表格与会签的官僚式折磨。

pos.zh: 官僚的；官僚作风的；程序繁琐的

derivatives.zh: 官僚体制（bureaucrat + -cy，由形容词所指的作风回指整套制度）
以官僚方式（bureaucratic + -ally，由性质转指方式）
官僚（bureau + -crat，由机构转指其中的人）
使官僚化（bureaucrat + -ize，由人转指使之成为那样的过程）

senses.title: Of a bureaucracy
senses.definition: relating to the offices and officials that carry out public business
senses.definitionCN: 与执行公共事务的机关及人员相关
senses.example: The report criticizes the bureaucratic chain that handles visas.
senses.exampleCN: 报告批评处理签证的那条官僚链条。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the noun to whatever it modifies, with no judgement yet.
senses.whyCN: 形容词先把名词接到被修饰者上，此时还没有评价。

senses.title: Weighed down by procedure
senses.definition: requiring many forms, signatures and approvals before anything happens
senses.definitionCN: 办事之前需要大量表格、签字与批准
senses.example: A bureaucratic approval can outlast the problem it was meant to solve.
senses.exampleCN: 一道官僚审批可能比它要解决的问题活得还久。
senses.why: because procedure is the visible surface of the apparatus, the adjective slid into naming its cost.
senses.whyCN: 程序是机关最可见的表面，因此形容词顺势用来指称它的代价。

senses.title: Hierarchical in structure
senses.definition: organized in ranks, where each level reports upward and approves downward
senses.definitionCN: 按等级组织，上级受汇报、下级受批准
senses.example: The agency's bureaucratic structure slowed every decision.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构的层级结构拖慢了每一个决定。
senses.why: rank is the skeleton of the noun, so the adjective can describe the shape alone.
senses.whyCN: 等级是名词的骨架，因此形容词可以只描述这个形状。

senses.title: By rule, not by case
senses.titleCN: 照章办事、不顾具体情形的
senses.definition: deciding by fixed rule even when the individual case plainly calls for an exception
senses.definitionCN: 即使个别情形明显需要变通，仍按固定规则处理
senses.example: A bureaucratic reading of the rule refused the refund.
senses.exampleCN: 对规则的照章解读拒绝了退款。
senses.why: the point of the rule is to treat like cases alike, and that virtue turns into a vice at the margins.
senses.whyCN: 规则的用意是同样情形同样处理，这一优点在边缘处变成了缺点。

senses.title: Written in official style
senses.definition: using the inflated, passive and noun-heavy style typical of official writing
senses.definitionCN: 使用公文常见的堆砌、被动与名词化文风
senses.example: The memo was so bureaucratic that its request vanished.
senses.exampleCN: 这份备忘录公文腔太重，其中的请求都消失了。
senses.why: style follows structure: writing that must pass many desks ends up addressing none of them.
senses.whyCN: 文风跟着结构走：必须经过许多桌面的文字，最后谁的账也不买。

senses.title: Overstaffed and layered
senses.definition: having more levels and staff than the work requires
senses.definitionCN: 层级与人员超出工作所需
senses.example: The ministry became bureaucratic long before it became effective.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部在变得有效之前很久就已变得臃肿。
senses.why: size is the noun's eighth sense, and the adjective can carry that criticism too.
senses.whyCN: 规模是名词的第八义，形容词同样可以带上这层批评。

senses.title: Impersonal
senses.titleCN: 非人格化的、不讲人情的
senses.definition: treating people as file numbers rather than as persons with circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 把人当作档案编号，而非有具体处境的人
senses.example: Her bureaucratic tone made the refusal sound pre-decided.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种非人格化的语气让拒绝听起来早已定好。
senses.why: impersonality is the neutral feature of rule by files, felt from the receiving side as coldness.
senses.whyCN: 非人格化本是按档案办事的中性特征，从接受一方感受即为冷淡。

senses.title: Of an official elite
senses.titleCN: 官僚阶层的、官僚精英的
senses.definition: belonging to career officials as a social group with its own interests
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为利益群体的职业官员
senses.example: Bureaucratic interests shaped the bill before it reached the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 官僚阶层的利益在法案上会之前就已塑形了它。
senses.why: once officials form a career corps, their shared outlook can be called bureaucratic.
senses.whyCN: 官员一旦形成职业群体，其共同心态便可称作官僚式的。

intro.en: Bureaucratic is bureaucracy plus the adjectival suffix -ic; bureaucracy itself was coined in French from bureau 'desk' and Greek kratos 'power'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bureaucratic 是 bureaucracy 加形容词后缀 -ic；bureaucracy 本身由法语 bureau「书桌」与希腊 kratos「力量」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kratos 'strength, might' produced -kratia 'rule', the suffix behind -cracy and -cratic.
items.cn: kratos「力量、强权」产生 -kratia「统治」，即 -cracy 与 -cratic 背后的后缀。

items.en: Bureaucratie was coined in French around the 1810s as a satirical name for rule by officials.
items.cn: bureaucratie 于 1810 年代前后在法语中造出，是对官员统治的讽刺称呼。

items.en: English borrowed bureaucracy in the nineteenth century, and the adjective bureaucratic followed in the same century.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪借入 bureaucracy，形容词 bureaucratic 也在同一世纪出现。

items.en: Weber's analysis gave the noun a neutral technical sense, and the adjective split between that neutral reading and the older complaint.
items.cn: 韦伯的分析给名词一个中性术语义，形容词则在中性读法与旧的抱怨读法之间一分为二。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact first appearance of the English adjective is not pinned down, and the origins of French burel and Greek kratos are both unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语形容词的确切首见未被确定；法语 burel 与希腊 kratos 的来源均无定论。

note.en: Group one shares the bureau or -cratic stock; group two holds adjectives for rules and officialdom.
note.cn: 第一组共享 bureau 或 -cratic 词干；第二组是关于规章与官场的形容词。

entries.definition: The system or body itself; the adjective describes something as having its marks.
entries.definitionCN: 指制度或机构本身；形容词则描述某物带有它的印记。

entries.definition: One official; the adjective can describe a tone or a procedure, not only a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指一位官员；形容词可描述语气或程序，不限于人。

entries.definition: Of rule by a single unrestricted ruler; it shares -cratic but not the desks and files.
entries.definitionCN: 指一人不受限制的统治；共享 -cratic，却无关书桌与档案。

entries.definition: Of rule or manners by a supposed best class; the suffix is shared, the root aristos is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指由所谓最优阶层统治或具有其风度；后缀共享，词根 aristos 不同。

entries.definition: Of management work in general, with no hint of excessive procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指管理工作，不含程序过度的暗示。

entries.definition: Approved by or belonging to an authority; bureaucratic points at method rather than authorization.
entries.definitionCN: 经权威批准或属于权威的；bureaucratic 指向方法而非授权。

entries.definition: Concerning the steps to be followed; it is narrower and can be neutral where bureaucratic is critical.
entries.definitionCN: 关于应遵循的步骤；范围更窄，且可为中性，而 bureaucratic 带批评。

entries.definition: Used before a noun for obstructive paperwork, harsher and more colloquial than bureaucratic.
entries.definitionCN: 置于名词前指阻碍性的文书，比 bureaucratic 更重、更口语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bureaucrat + -ic: having the marks of the desk-and-stamp order.
normal.cn: bureaucrat + -ic：带有书桌与印章秩序的特征。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the complaint: bureaucratic delay, bureaucratic hurdles, bureaucratic inertia.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出抱怨：官僚拖延、官僚障碍、官僚惰性。

normal.en: The adverb bureaucratically names the manner: decided bureaucratically.
normal.cn: 副词 bureaucratically 指方式：以官僚方式决定。

normal.en: -cratic recurs in democratic, aristocratic and autocratic, all from Greek kratos.
normal.cn: -cratic 反复出现于 democratic、aristocratic、autocratic，皆出希腊 kratos。

normal.en: Compare the pair: a bureaucracy is the body, bureaucratic is the smell it leaves.
normal.cn: 对照这一对：bureaucracy 是那个机构，bureaucratic 是它留下的气味。

abstract.en: Picture a door that asks for a form to request the key to the room with the forms.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，要先填表才能拿到存放表格那间屋子的钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence written only in the passive voice, so that nobody is doing anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一句全用被动语态写成的话，结果谁也没在做任何事。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler that measures people but refuses to measure itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只量别人、从不量自己的尺。

examples.en: The permit process was bureaucratic to the point of absurdity.
examples.cn: 许可流程官僚到荒唐的地步。

examples.en: Her bureaucratic reply answered the form, not the question.
examples.cn: 她那官僚式的回复答的是表格，不是问题。

examples.en: Reformers targeted the bureaucratic layers above the laboratory.
examples.cn: 改革者对准了实验室之上的官僚层级。

dict_mnemonic.text: bureau（办公桌）+ crat（掌权者）+ ic（……的）＝ 桌后掌权者那一套的；记「章多、层多、话冷」。

root: bureau + -crat + -ic：bureau 源自法语「书桌、办公室」（其布料义 burel 来源不确定），-crat 与 -cratic 经希腊 -kratia 上溯 kratos「力量」，其希腊语之前的来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from neutral description to complaint: belonging to the offices, costly procedure, rank, rule without exception, official prose, overstaffing, coldness, and the outlook of a career corps.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从中性描述走向抱怨：属于机关、程序代价、等级、不讲例外、公文腔、人浮于事、冷淡、以及职业官员群体的心态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a form travelling between desks, each adding a requirement and none taking responsibility.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份表格在桌面间旅行，每张桌面加一项要求，却无人负责。

branches.en: FROM LABEL TO COMPLAINT: first merely of the offices, then of what their procedure costs.
branches.cn: 从标签到抱怨：先说属于机关，再说程序带来的代价。

branches.en: SKELETON: rank is the structure that makes the rest possible.
branches.cn: 骨架：等级是让其余一切得以发生的结构。

branches.en: RULE AND ITS VOICE: deciding without exception, then writing in the style that hides the decider.
branches.cn: 规则与其嗓音：不讲例外地决定，再用掩盖决定者的文风书写。

branches.en: BODY AND CLASS: too many levels, and a career corps with its own interests.
branches.cn: 身躯与阶层：层级过多，以及一个有自身利益的职业群体。

branches.en: THE RECEIVING SIDE: impersonality felt as coldness.
branches.cn: 接受的一端：非人格化被感受为冷淡。

intro.en: Bureaucratic is a three-part build: French bureau, Greek -kratia and the English suffix -ic, each still productive.
intro.cn: bureaucratic 由三部分构成：法语 bureau、希腊 -kratia 与英语后缀 -ic，三者至今仍有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element is Latin-mediated, coming from Greek kratos; bureau and -ic are French and English respectively.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第二部分经拉丁中介，来自希腊 kratos；bureau 与 -ic 分别属法语和英语。

items.example: The bureau issued the licence.
items.exampleCN: 该局签发了执照。

items.meaning: one who rules or holds office
items.example: A bureaucrat holds a desk, not a throne.
items.exampleCN: 官僚坐的是书桌，不是王座。

items.example: Democratic and aristocratic share this ending.
items.exampleCN: democratic 与 aristocratic 共享这一词尾。

items.example: Bureaucratic adds this suffix to the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: bureaucratic 就是在这个名词词干上加此后缀。

items.example: The bureaucrat asked for another copy.
items.exampleCN: 那位官员又要了一份复印件。

items.example: Bureaucracy outlived three ministers.
items.exampleCN: 官僚体制比三任部长都活得久。

items.example: The case was settled bureaucratically.
items.exampleCN: 此案以官僚方式了结。

items.example: Bureaucratese hides who decided what.
items.exampleCN: 公文腔掩盖了谁决定了什么。

definition_zh: 治理；治理方式；治理结构；（公司、数据等领域的）治理机制
definition_en: the way an organization or society is directed and held to account, including its rules and decision-making structures
core_image: 一张长桌，代表们按程序发言、表决、记录，散会后留下的是可被追问的决定
scene: 董事会按既定程序审议预算，投完票后把异议一并记入会议记录。Governance leaves a paper trail that any outsider can follow.
sceneCN: 这里 governance 指使决定可被追问的那套治理方式（第 1 个义项：作为整体实践）；句意为治理会留下任何外部人都能追查的书面线索。

pos.zh: 治理；治理方式（不可数，指过程与机制；作可数时指某种治理安排）

derivatives.zh: 统治；支配（拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」，由操船转指操持事务）
州长；管理者（govern + -or「行事者」，由动作转指人）
政府；政体（govern + -ment「结果或机构」，由动作转指机关）
可治理的（govern + -able「可被」，由动作转指可能性）

senses.title: Direction of a society
senses.definition: the whole practice of steering public affairs, including rules, institutions and accountability
senses.definitionCN: 引导公共事务的整体实践，含规则、机构与问责
senses.example: Governance is judged by outcomes, not by org charts.
senses.exampleCN: 治理的好坏看结果，不看组织架构图。
senses.why: the suffix -ance names an activity rather than an office, so governance points at the doing of rule.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ance 指活动而非机关，因此 governance 指向统治的进行过程。

senses.title: Corporate governance
senses.definition: the system by which a company's board, managers and shareholders are balanced and held to account
senses.definitionCN: 平衡并约束董事会、管理层与股东的制度安排
senses.example: Corporate governance determines who may overrule the chief executive.
senses.exampleCN: 公司治理决定谁能否决首席执行官。
senses.why: once the word detached from the state, companies borrowed it for their own internal checks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦脱离国家，公司便借它来指自身的内部制衡。

senses.title: The machinery of rules
senses.definition: the specific bodies, procedures and reporting lines through which decisions are made
senses.definitionCN: 做出决定所依的具体机构、程序与汇报线
senses.example: The treaty created a governance structure with three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约建立了含三个委员会的治理结构。
senses.why: structure is what makes a practice repeatable, so governance often names the arrangement rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: 结构让实践可重复，因此 governance 常指安排而非行为。

senses.title: How public affairs are handled
senses.definition: the style and quality of public administration, whether open, lawful and responsive or not
senses.definitionCN: 公共行政的风格与品质，是否公开、依法、有回应
senses.example: Poor governance shows up first as missing records.
senses.exampleCN: 治理不佳最先表现为记录缺失。
senses.why: the word lets observers compare systems without naming a government or a party.
senses.whyCN: 这个词让观察者比较不同体制，而不必点名某个政府或政党。

senses.title: Good governance as a standard
senses.definition: a donor and policy standard combining transparency, rule of law, participation and effectiveness
senses.definitionCN: 由透明、法治、参与与效能构成的援助与政策标准
senses.example: Loans were tied to good governance benchmarks.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款与善治指标挂钩。
senses.why: aid agencies needed a measurable word that could attach to conditions, and governance filled it.
senses.whyCN: 援助机构需要一个可量化、能附条件的词，governance 正好填空。

senses.title: Global governance
senses.definition: the informal and formal arrangements by which states and bodies manage shared problems without a world state
senses.definitionCN: 各国与各机构在没有世界政府的情况下管理共同问题的正式与非正式安排
senses.example: Climate talks are a test case of global governance.
senses.exampleCN: 气候谈判是全球治理的一个试验场。
senses.why: problems cross borders while authority does not, so the word was stretched above the state.
senses.whyCN: 问题跨境而权威不跨境，于是这个词被拉到国家之上。

senses.title: Governance of data and systems
senses.definition: the rules deciding who may collect, access, change and delete an organization's information
senses.definitionCN: 决定谁能收集、访问、修改与删除组织信息的规则
senses.example: Data governance decides who may delete a customer record.
senses.exampleCN: 数据治理决定谁能删除客户记录。
senses.why: the newest extension keeps the core idea of accountable control while dropping the state entirely.
senses.whyCN: 最新引申保留了「可问责的控制」这一内核，却完全去掉了国家。

senses.title: Exercise of governing authority
senses.definition: the actual wielding of authority, as distinct from the institutions that hold it
senses.definitionCN: 权威的实际行使，区别于持有权威的机构
senses.example: Authority was clear on paper; governance in practice was improvised.
senses.exampleCN: 纸面上的权责很清楚，实际的治理却是临时应付。
senses.why: the older abstract sense survives: governance is what happens when authority is used, not merely where it sits.
senses.whyCN: 更早的抽象义仍在：治理是权威被使用时的情形，而不只是它所在的位置。

intro.en: Governance comes from Old French governer, from Latin gubernare 'to steer a ship', itself borrowed from Greek kybernan 'to steer'. The -ance suffix names the activity. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: governance 来自古法语 governer，上溯拉丁 gubernare「操船」，后者借自希腊 kybernan「掌舵」。-ance 后缀指这一活动。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kybernan meant 'to steer, pilot a ship', and its metaphorical use for guiding people is already Greek.
items.cn: kybernan 意为「掌舵、操船」，以之隐喻引导人，在希腊语中已然存在。

items.en: Latin took the verb as gubernare 'to steer, direct, rule', and gubernator named the helmsman and then a governor.
items.cn: 拉丁语取来作 gubernare「操船、指引、统治」，gubernator 既指舵手也指治理者。

items.en: Old French governer carried it into English in the thirteenth century, first as a verb of steering and directing.
items.cn: 古法语 governer 在 13 世纪把它带入英语，最初是操船与指引的动词。

items.en: Governance appeared later as the abstract noun of the act, parallel to government, which named the body rather than the doing.
items.cn: governance 较晚出现，是这一行为的抽象名词，与指机关而非行为的 government 并行。

items.en: In the late twentieth century governance spread to corporate boards, global institutions and data systems, always keeping accountability at its centre.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期 governance 扩展到公司董事会、全球机构与数据系统，始终以问责为核心。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek origin of kybernan is not established, and the forms proposed for it are reconstructions rather than demonstrated ancestors.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：kybernan 在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，为其提出的形式属重构形式，而非已证的祖先。

note.en: Group one shares the govern root; group two holds near neighbours in public management.
note.cn: 第一组共享 govern 词根；第二组是公共管理领域的近义词。

entries.definition: The institutions that hold authority, formed with -ment 'result, means'; governance is the activity those institutions perform.
entries.definitionCN: 持有权威的机构，由 -ment「结果、手段」构成；governance 是这些机构所进行的活动。

entries.definition: To steer or rule directly; the noun shifts attention from the actor to the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 直接操持或统治；名词把注意力从行动者移到安排上。

entries.definition: One who governs a province, state or institution; it names a holder of office, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 治理一省、一州或一机构的人；指任职者，而非过程。

entries.definition: Of a governor, from the same Latin gubernator; it looks unlike govern but shares the helmsman image.
entries.definitionCN: 指州长的，同出拉丁 gubernator；形似无关，却共享舵手意象。

entries.definition: The execution of policy by staff; governance adds accountability and the rule-setting level above execution.
entries.definitionCN: 由人员执行政策；governance 另加问责与执行之上的定规层面。

entries.definition: The everyday running of an organization's work; governance concerns who may direct and how they answer for it.
entries.definitionCN: 组织日常工作的运转；governance 关注谁有权指挥以及如何为此负责。

entries.definition: The specific rules imposed on an activity; governance is the wider frame that produces and enforces them.
entries.definitionCN: 施加于某项活动的具体规则；governance 是产生并执行它们的更宽框架。

entries.definition: Responsible care of something entrusted to one, close to governance in tone but without the machinery of office.
entries.definitionCN: 对所托付之物的负责照管，语气接近 governance，但不含机关机器。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: govern + -ance: the doing of steering, not the steering body.
normal.cn: govern + -ance：掌舵这件事，而非掌舵的机构。

normal.en: Latin gubernare is a ship's helm, so governance keeps the image of a hand on the tiller.
normal.cn: 拉丁 gubernare 是船舵，因此 governance 始终带着一只手扶舵的画面。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: corporate governance, global governance, data governance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：公司治理、全球治理、数据治理。

normal.en: The family runs govern, governor, government, governable, gubernatorial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 govern、governor、government、governable、gubernatorial。

normal.en: Accountability is the test word: if nobody can be asked why, it is not governance.
normal.cn: 问责是试金石：若无人可被追问缘由，那就不算治理。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a tiller while the crew argues about the course.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着舵，船员们同时在争论航向。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting that ends with a minute anyone can later read.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会开完留下一份谁都能日后查阅的记录。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook whose authors must sign each page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册，每一页都要作者签名。

examples.en: The fund tied its grants to improvements in local governance.
examples.cn: 该基金把拨款与地方治理的改善挂钩。

examples.en: Corporate governance failed long before the share price fell.
examples.cn: 公司治理在股价下跌之前很久就已失灵。

examples.en: Data governance decides who may read the archive.
examples.cn: 数据治理决定谁可以读取档案。

dict_mnemonic.text: govern（掌舵）+ ance（行为）＝ 掌舵这件事；记「船往哪开、谁在扶舵、事后谁解释」。

root: 古法语 governer ← 拉丁 gubernare「操船、治理」← 希腊 kybernan「掌舵」；kybernan 在希腊语之前的来源不确定，相关更早形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand on a tiller: steering a society, steering a company, the frame that makes steering repeatable, the quality of the steering, its policy standard, its global stretch, its newest data form, and the plain exercise of authority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一只手扶舵展开：引导社会、引导公司、使引导可重复的框架、引导的品质、其政策标准、其全球延伸、其最新的数据形态，以及权威的单纯行使。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a tiller, a course agreed in public, and a record that lets others ask why.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶着舵，航向公开商定，还留下可供他人追问缘由的记录。

branches.en: THE ACT ITSELF: steering a society, and the bare wielding of authority.
branches.cn: 行为本身：引导社会，以及权威的单纯行使。

branches.en: THE COMPANY VERSION: the same helm inside a firm.
branches.cn: 公司版本：同一副舵搬进企业内部。

branches.en: THE FRAME: bodies and reporting lines make steering repeatable.
branches.cn: 框架：机构与汇报线让引导可以重复。

branches.en: QUALITY AND YARDSTICK: how well it steers, then the standard used to grade it.
branches.cn: 品质与标尺：先问掌舵好不好，再给出评分标准。

branches.en: TWO NEW DOMAINS: above the state, and inside the database.
branches.cn: 两个新领域：国家之上，以及数据库之内。

intro.en: Governance is govern plus -ance, and govern itself is a Latin borrowing ultimately from a Greek verb of steering.
intro.cn: governance 是 govern 加 -ance，而 govern 本身是源自希腊掌舵动词的拉丁借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gubernare and gubernator give govern, governor, government and gubernatorial; the ship's helm is the shared image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gubernare 与 gubernator 衍生 govern、governor、government、gubernatorial；共同的意象是船舵。

items.example: The verb began at the helm.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词从舵柄开始。

items.example: The gubernator held the course.
items.exampleCN: 舵手守着航向。

items.example: Rules govern the use of the archive.
items.exampleCN: 规则支配档案的使用。

items.meaning: the activity of steering and answering for it
items.meaningCN: 掌舵并为此负责的活动
items.example: Governance decides who may speak for the board.
items.exampleCN: 治理决定谁能代表董事会发言。

items.example: The government changed after the vote.
items.exampleCN: 投票之后政府更替。

items.example: The governor signed the order.
items.exampleCN: 州长签署了这道命令。

items.example: A governable city keeps its records.
items.exampleCN: 可治理的城市会保留记录。

items.meaning: the state or activity of doing
items.example: Governance and guidance share this ending.
items.exampleCN: governance 与 guidance 共享这一词尾。

definition_zh: 统治；管理；支配；决定；约束；控制（情绪等）
definition_en: to direct and control the affairs of a state, an institution, or a process, usually by rules or authority
core_image: 舵手握着舵柄，风从侧面来，他不断微调角度，让船沿着既定航线走
scene: 风向变了三次，舵手每次都只轻轻转一点，船始终没有偏离航线。A handful of rules govern the whole exchange of records.
sceneCN: 这里 govern 指以规则来支配、决定某事的进行（第 3 个义项：决定、支配）；句意为少数几条规则支配着整条记录交换流程。

pos.zh: 统治；治理；管理
支配；决定；制约
控制；抑制（情绪、行为）

derivatives.zh: 政府（govern + -ment「结果、机构」，由动作转指机关）
州长；管理者（govern + -or「行事者」，由动作转指人）
治理（govern + -ance「活动」，由动作转指过程本身）
无法治理的（un-「不」+ governable，由可治理转指其反面）

senses.title: Rule a state
senses.definition: to hold and exercise authority over a country or people
senses.definitionCN: 对国家或民众持有并行使权威
senses.example: The council governed the city for two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 该议会治理这座城市长达两代人。
senses.why: the oldest sense is the helm: someone takes the tiller of a whole community.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是舵柄：有人接过整个社群的舵。

senses.title: Run an institution
senses.definition: to direct the affairs of a school, company or committee
senses.definitionCN: 主持学校、公司或委员会的事务
senses.example: A board of trustees governs the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 一个理事会管理这座博物馆。
senses.why: the same authority was scaled down from a people to an organization.
senses.whyCN: 同一套权威从一国民众缩小到一个组织。

senses.title: Determine how something works
senses.definition: to be the factor or principle that determines an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 成为决定某个结果的因素或原则
senses.example: A handful of rules govern the whole exchange of records.
senses.exampleCN: 少数几条规则支配着整条记录交换流程。
senses.why: here the governor is not a person but a rule that steers events as surely as a hand steers a ship.
senses.whyCN: 这里的治理者不是人，而是一条像手操舵那样确实引导事件的规则。

senses.title: Restrain by rule
senses.definition: to limit conduct by an authoritative rule or law
senses.definitionCN: 以有权威的规则或法律限制行为
senses.example: Strict codes govern the disposal of clinical waste.
senses.exampleCN: 严格的规范约束着临床废物的处置。
senses.why: to govern is also to keep within bounds, which is the same steering applied to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 治理也意味着把人留在界线之内，那是同一套操舵施加于行为。

senses.title: Control oneself
senses.titleCN: 控制自己的情绪或举动
senses.definition: to keep an impulse or emotion under deliberate restraint
senses.definitionCN: 有意把冲动或情绪压住
senses.example: He governed his anger until the meeting ended.
senses.exampleCN: 他把怒气压到会议结束。
senses.why: the metaphor turns inward: the self is both the ship and the crew that must keep it on course.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻转向内部：自我既是船，也是必须让它不偏航的船员。

senses.title: Regulate a machine or rate
senses.definition: to control the speed or operation of a device by a regulator
senses.definitionCN: 用调节装置控制装置的速度或运转
senses.example: A centrifugal device governs the engine's speed.
senses.exampleCN: 一个离心装置调节发动机的转速。
senses.why: engineering kept the literal helm sense, where governing is mechanical adjustment rather than command.
senses.whyCN: 工程学保留了字面的舵义：治理在这里是机械调节，而非发号施令。

senses.title: Take a case in grammar
senses.definition: to require a particular case or form in the following word
senses.definitionCN: 要求后接词取某一特定格或形式
senses.example: In Latin a preposition governs the case of its object.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语中前置词支配其宾语的格。
senses.why: the older grammatical sense treats a word as holding authority over its neighbour's form.
senses.whyCN: 较早的语法义把一个词当作对邻词形式持有权威者。

senses.title: Guide and lead
senses.definition: to guide a process or group toward an intended end
senses.definitionCN: 把某个过程或群体引向既定目标
senses.example: She governed the negotiations toward a single draft.
senses.exampleCN: 她把谈判引向一份统一草案。
senses.why: before it was an office, governing was simply steering, and that plain sense survives in guidance.
senses.whyCN: 在成为官职之前，治理只是操舵，这个朴素义在「引导」中留存。

intro.en: Govern comes through Old French governer from Latin gubernare 'to steer, pilot', borrowed from Greek kybernan 'to steer'. The ship's helm is the original image. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: govern 经古法语 governer 上溯拉丁 gubernare「操船、掌舵」，后者借自希腊 kybernan「掌舵」。船舵是原始意象。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kybernan meant 'to steer a ship', and the metaphor of steering a city or a people is already present in Greek prose.
items.cn: kybernan 意为「操船」，而把城邦或民众比作操船，在希腊散文里已然存在。

items.en: Latin gubernare kept both the literal and the political sense, and gubernator named the helmsman first and the governor second.
items.cn: 拉丁 gubernare 兼有字面义与政治义，gubernator 先指舵手，后指治理者。

items.en: Old French governer brought the verb to English in the thirteenth century, where it soon covered rule, management and restraint.
items.cn: 古法语 governer 在 13 世纪把该动词带入英语，很快兼指统治、管理与约束。

items.en: School grammar extended govern to the relation of a word to the case of the word it controls, a usage still current in traditional grammar.
items.cn: 学校语法把 govern 扩展到词与其所控制之词的格的关系，这一用法在传统语法中仍存。

items.en: Engineering applied the word to regulators that hold an engine at a steady speed, reviving the literal helm.
items.cn: 工程学把这个词用于把发动机稳定在某一转速的调节器，等于复活了字面的舵义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek origin of kybernan is not established, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated ancestor.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：kybernan 在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，为其提出的任何印欧形式均属重构形式，而非已证的祖先。

note.en: Group one shares the helm root; group two holds verbs of ruling and controlling.
note.cn: 第一组共享舵柄词根；第二组是统治与控制的动词。

entries.definition: The body that holds authority; the verb names the activity, so government cannot replace govern in a sentence about deciding outcomes.
entries.definitionCN: 持有权威的机关；动词指活动，因此在谈论决定结果的句子里 government 不能替代 govern。

entries.definition: The arrangement and quality of directing, not a single act; govern is the plain verb behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 引导的安排与品质，而非单个动作；govern 是它背后朴素的动词。

entries.definition: One who governs a province or institution, and also a mechanical regulator, so it keeps the helm image twice.
entries.definitionCN: 治理一省或一机构的人，也指机械调节器，因此两度保留舵的意象。

entries.definition: Of a governor, from Latin gubernator; it looks unrelated to govern but descends from the same helmsman.
entries.definitionCN: 指州长的，来自拉丁 gubernator；看着与 govern 无关，却同出同一个舵手。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for holding power over people; govern suggests steering and administration rather than mere command.
entries.definitionCN: 指对人握有权力，最日常的说法；govern 更带操舵与行政之意，而非单纯命令。

entries.definition: To put policy and institutions into operation; it lacks the steering image and the sense of determining outcomes.
entries.definitionCN: 把政策与机构付诸运转；缺少操舵意象与决定结果之义。

entries.definition: To control by explicit rules, often a narrower and more technical activity than governing.
entries.definitionCN: 以明确规则控制，通常比 govern 更窄、更技术化。

entries.definition: To keep something within limits, including emotions and machines; it overlaps the later senses of govern but not the political one.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物留在限度内，包括情绪与机器；与 govern 的后几个义项交叠，但不含政治义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek kybernan 'steer': governing is holding the tiller of something larger than oneself.
normal.cn: 希腊 kybernan「掌舵」：治理就是替比自己更大的东西扶舵。

normal.en: The family runs govern, government, governor, governance, governable, gubernatorial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 govern、government、governor、governance、governable、gubernatorial。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: govern a country, rules that govern trade, govern one's temper.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出义项：治理国家、支配贸易的规则、控制脾气。

normal.en: The passive turn is common: the factors governing demand, the law governing mergers.
normal.cn: 被动式说法很常见：决定需求的因素、管辖并购的法律。

normal.en: The regulator in an engine is called a governor, which returns the word to its helm.
normal.cn: 发动机的调节器叫 governor，等于把这个词送回舵柄。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that never moves much, only enough to keep the boat off the rocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手几乎不动，只动到足以让船不触礁。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that behaves like a rudder: invisible until something drifts.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则像舵一样：不出事时看不见，一漂就显形。

abstract.en: Picture a person holding their own wrist to stop themselves from speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人握住自己的手腕，好让自己别开口。

examples.en: Traditional councils still govern the valley's grazing rights.
examples.cn: 传统议事会仍管理着山谷的放牧权。

examples.en: Two principles govern how the samples are stored.
examples.cn: 有两条原则决定样本如何存放。

examples.en: She governed her voice and answered in one flat sentence.
examples.cn: 她控制住声音，用一句平淡的话作答。

dict_mnemonic.text: govern＝握舵：管国家是掌大舵，管机构是掌小舵，管脾气是管自己的舵。

root: 古法语 governer ← 拉丁 gubernare「操船、治理」← 希腊 kybernan「掌舵」；kybernan 的更早来源不确定，相关印欧形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one tiller: ruling a people, running an institution, letting a rule steer events, restraining conduct, restraining oneself, adjusting a machine, holding grammatical authority, and simply guiding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一具舵柄展开：统治民众、主持机构、让规则引导事件、约束行为、约束自己、调节机器、在语法上支配，以及单纯的引导。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand making small corrections on a tiller while the wind keeps changing.
core.cn: 核心意象：风不断变向，一只手在舵柄上不断作很小的修正。

branches.en: SCALE: the same hand on a nation's tiller and on a museum's.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一只手，既扶国家的舵，也扶博物馆的舵。

branches.en: THE RULE TAKES THE TILLER: no person, only a principle deciding outcomes.
branches.cn: 规则接舵：没有人，只有一条原则在决定结果。

branches.en: BOUNDS OUTWARD AND INWARD: conduct restrained by rule, then impulse restrained by will.
branches.cn: 向外的界与向内的界：行为受规则约束，冲动受意志约束。

branches.en: THE LITERAL RETURN: a governor on an engine is a helm made of metal.
branches.cn: 字面回归：发动机上的调节器就是一具金属舵。

branches.en: AUTHORITY WITHOUT A STATE: a word holding a case, and a guide holding a course.
branches.cn: 没有国家的权威：一个词支配格，一个引导者守住航向。

intro.en: Govern is a Latin verb taken over through French; its prefixes and suffixes still build a large English family around the image of a helm.
intro.cn: govern 是经法语传入的拉丁动词，其前后缀至今围绕舵的意象构成一个不小的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gubernare and gubernator yield govern, governor, government, governance and gubernatorial; the -ern ending is not a living English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gubernare 与 gubernator 衍生 govern、governor、government、governance、gubernatorial；-ern 词尾不是活的英语后缀。

items.example: The Latin verb is a ship's helm.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词就是一具船舵。

items.example: Codes govern the storage of samples.
items.exampleCN: 规范约束样本的存放。

items.meaning: the result or body of an action
items.example: Government is the body, not the act.
items.exampleCN: government 指机关，不指行为。

items.example: Governance rests on records.
items.exampleCN: 治理靠记录立足。

items.example: The governor of the engine spins faster.
items.exampleCN: 发动机的调节器转得更快。

items.example: The district stayed governable.
items.exampleCN: 该地区始终可治。

items.example: The crowd became ungovernable.
items.exampleCN: 人群变得无法控制。

items.example: A gubernatorial race begins early.
items.exampleCN: 州长选战开始得早。

definition_zh: 政府；政体；治理行为；（英式）内阁、当权者；一届政府
definition_en: the group of people and institutions that direct a state, or the system by which a state is directed
core_image: 一栋办公楼里，部长们在长桌前签署文件，门外是等待答复的市民与记者
scene: 选票清点完毕的第二天，各部门才把拖欠已久的数字挂到网站上。The government published the figures only after the votes were counted.
sceneCN: 这里 government 指掌握行政权的政府机关（第 1 个义项：作为机构整体）；句意为政府直到计票结束之后才公布那些数字。

pos.zh: 政府；政体（可数，指一届政府或一种政体；不可数，指治理这件事）
（英式）内阁；当权者
（古）自制；自我约束

derivatives.zh: 政府的（government + -al「……的」，由机关转指其属性）
统治；治理（拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」，由动作本身指操持事务）
治理（govern + -ance「活动」，由机关转指过程）
反政府的（anti-「反对」+ government，由机关转指对立立场）

senses.title: The governing institutions
senses.definition: the body of institutions that direct public affairs and hold executive authority
senses.definitionCN: 主导公共事务并持有行政权威的整套机构
senses.example: The government employs a third of the town's adults.
senses.exampleCN: 政府雇用了镇上三分之一的成年人。
senses.why: -ment first named the result of governing, and the result came to mean the body that does it.
senses.whyCN: -ment 先指治理的结果，结果义再转指做出这个结果的机关。

senses.title: The form of rule
senses.definition: the system by which a state is organized, such as a monarchy or a republic
senses.definitionCN: 组织国家的制度，如君主制或共和制
senses.example: They compared two forms of government across the same century.
senses.exampleCN: 他们比较了同一世纪里的两种政体。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the older meaning of direction as a system rather than a set of persons.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了较早的意思：治理是一套制度，而非一群人。

senses.title: The act of governing
senses.definition: the activity of directing a state, as distinct from the bodies that carry it out
senses.definitionCN: 主导国家的活动，区别于执行它的机构
senses.example: Good government is measured in decades, not in news cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 治理的好坏以十年计，不以新闻周期计。
senses.why: English kept the action reading alongside the institutional one, so the word can name a practice.
senses.whyCN: 英语把行为义与机构义并存下来，因此这个词也能指一种实践。

senses.title: The ministers in office
senses.definition: in parliamentary usage, the prime minister and the ministers currently in office
senses.definitionCN: 在议会制用法中，指在任的首相与各部部长
senses.example: The government lost the motion by four votes.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁以四票之差输掉了动议。
senses.why: in a parliamentary system the executive sits inside the legislature, so the word narrowed to the ministers.
senses.whyCN: 在议会制中行政权坐于立法机关之内，于是这个词收窄为各部部长。

senses.title: One administration
senses.definition: a particular team holding office between one election and the next
senses.definitionCN: 在一次选举与下一次选举之间任职的特定班底
senses.example: Three governments fell within two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年内倒掉了三届政府。
senses.why: counting administrations requires a countable noun, and this sense supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 要数「届」，就需要一个可数名词，这个义项正好提供。

senses.title: State intervention
senses.titleCN: 政府对经济与社会的干预
senses.definition: the scope of the state's active role in the economy and in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 国家在经济与日常生活中主动介入的范围
senses.example: Arguments about big government are arguments about that scope.
senses.exampleCN: 关于大政府的争论，就是关于这个范围的争论。
senses.why: the word can stand for the state's reach, which is what political argument actually disputes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以代表国家触及的范围，而政治争论争的正是这个范围。

senses.title: Self-command
senses.definition: the old sense of holding one's own conduct under control
senses.definitionCN: 把自身行为置于控制之下的旧义
senses.example: The old manuals praised government of the passions.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手册称赞对激情的自制。
senses.why: the helm image once pointed inward too, and the dictionaries record this sense from the sixteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 舵的意象也曾指向内部，词典自 16 世纪起收录此义。

senses.title: Issued by official authority
senses.titleCN: 作为修饰语：官方的、政府签发的
senses.definition: used before a noun for something issued or owned by the state
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指由国家签发或持有的
senses.example: Government buildings line the avenue.
senses.exampleCN: 大道两旁都是政府建筑。
senses.why: attributive use lets the noun mark the source of a thing, a very common English pattern.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法让这个名词标示某物的来源，是英语中极常见的模式。

intro.en: Government is govern plus the Latin-derived suffix -ment, modelled on French gouvernement. The suffix first meant the result or means of an action, then the body that performs it. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: government 是 govern 加拉丁系后缀 -ment，仿法语 gouvernement 构成。该后缀先指动作的结果或手段，再指执行动作的机关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gubernare 'to steer a ship' supplied the verb, and its metaphorical sense of directing people was already Latin.
items.cn: gubernare「操船」提供了动词，其「引导人」的隐喻义在拉丁语中已有。

items.en: Old French gouvernement meant 'administration, direction' in the fourteenth century, with the stress on the activity.
items.cn: 古法语 gouvernement 在 14 世纪指「管理、指引」，重心在活动本身。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century as the act of governing, keeping the abstract sense alive beside the concrete one.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入，指治理这一行为，使抽象义与具体义并存。

items.en: By the sixteenth century government commonly named the persons and bodies that rule, a shift from doing to the doers.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，government 常指统治的人与机关，重心从「做」转到「做的人」。

items.en: In parliamentary usage the word narrowed further to the ministers in office, while American usage kept it for the whole executive branch.
items.cn: 在议会制用法中，这个词进一步收窄为在任部长；美式用法则保留指整个行政部门。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation for the institutional sense is not precisely dated, and the pre-Greek origin of the steering verb behind gubernare is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：机构义的最早英语书证没有确切年代；gubernare 背后那个操船动词在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one shares the govern stem; group two holds words for the state and for rule.
note.cn: 第一组共享 govern 词干；第二组是关于国家与统治的词。

entries.definition: The practice and quality of directing, including accountability; government names the body that holds authority.
entries.definitionCN: 引导的实践与品质，含问责；government 指持有权威的机关。

entries.definition: To direct or rule; the noun adds the institutional result of that activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指引或统治；名词加上这一活动所形成的机构结果。

entries.definition: A single official heading a state or institution; it names one seat, not the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 领导一州或一机构的单个官员；指一个席位，而非整体。

entries.definition: Of a governor, from Latin gubernator; the form looks foreign but belongs to the same helm family.
entries.definitionCN: 指州长的，来自拉丁 gubernator；词形看着陌生，却属同一个舵的词族。

entries.definition: The political entity as a whole, including territory and people; government is only its directing apparatus.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的政治实体，含领土与人民；government 只是它的主导机关。

entries.definition: In American usage a president's team in office; elsewhere it means management, so it is narrower than government.
entries.definitionCN: 美式用法指总统的执政班底；其他地方指管理，因此比 government 更窄。

entries.definition: A system of rule, often with a hint of harshness or of recent imposition; government is the plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 一套统治秩序，常暗含严苛或新近强加之意；government 是更中性的说法。

entries.definition: The legal or accepted power to act; government is the body that normally holds such power.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的法律或公认权力；government 通常就是持有此种权力的机关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: govern + -ment: first the result of steering, then the body that steers.
normal.cn: govern + -ment：先是操舵的结果，再是操舵的机关。

normal.en: The family runs govern, government, governor, governance, governmental.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 govern、government、governor、governance、governmental。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: form a government, coalition government, local government.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：组阁、联合政府、地方政府。

normal.en: Countable and uncountable split matters: three governments fell, but government is necessary.
normal.cn: 可数与否的分野很关键：倒了三届政府，但治理本身是必要的。

normal.en: British news says the government lost the vote; American news says the administration did.
normal.cn: 英媒说内阁输掉表决，美媒说执政班底输掉表决。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where the same five people sign for a whole country.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，同样五个人替整个国家签字。

abstract.en: Picture a building that changes tenants but keeps the same letterhead.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼换了租客，信笺抬头却始终不变。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a tiller that must answer to a queue outside the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着舵，还得向门外的队列交代。

examples.en: The government raised the levy without warning the growers.
examples.cn: 政府加征费用，却没有事先通知种植者。

examples.en: Coalition governments tend to postpone unpopular decisions.
examples.cn: 联合政府往往把不得人心的决定往后拖。

examples.en: Local government carries most of the cost of the repairs.
examples.cn: 地方政府承担了修缮的大部分费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: govern（掌舵）+ ment（机构）＝ 替国家扶舵的那套班子；记「换班子不换舵」。

root: govern + -ment：govern 经古法语 governer 上溯拉丁 gubernare「操船、治理」，再上溯希腊 kybernan「掌舵」，后者更早来源不确定；-ment 源自拉丁 -mentum「结果、手段」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one helm through time: the act of steering, the system of steering, the body that steers, the ministers inside that body, one team in office, the state's reach, steering oneself, and the attributive mark of official origin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一具舵柄穿过时间：操舵的行为、操舵的制度、操舵的机关、机关里的部长、一届执政班底、国家触及的范围、对自己操舵，以及标示官方来源的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a national tiller, inside a building that outsiders stand outside of.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶着国家的舵，人在一栋楼里，外人站在楼外。

branches.en: DOING AND DOERS: the practice and the body are the same word seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 做与做的人：实践与机关是同一个词的两面。

branches.en: THE RULEBOOK: the form of rule outlives every team that works it.
branches.cn: 规则书：政体比任何操作它的班底都活得久。

branches.en: INSIDE THE BUILDING: the ministers, then the particular team counting as one unit.
branches.cn: 楼内：先是部长们，再是被算作一个单位的特定班底。

branches.en: REACH: how far the state's hand extends into the economy.
branches.cn: 触及范围：国家这只手伸进经济多深。

branches.en: INWARD AND ADJECTIVAL: steering oneself, and marking a thing as officially issued.
branches.cn: 向内与定语：对自己操舵，以及标示某物由官方签发。

intro.en: Government is one Latin verb plus one Latin suffix, and both parts build a large English family.
intro.cn: government 是一个拉丁动词加一个拉丁后缀，两部分都构成不小的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Gubernare yields govern, governor and gubernatorial; -mentum yields government, argument and monument.
latinIntro.cn: gubernare 衍生 govern、governor、gubernatorial；-mentum 衍生 government、argument、monument。

items.example: The verb pictures a hand on the helm.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词画出扶舵的手。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: Government began as the result of governing.
items.exampleCN: government 本指治理的结果。

items.example: Ministers govern with borrowed authority.
items.exampleCN: 部长们凭借来的权威治理。

items.meaning: the body that directs a state
items.example: The government fell after the budget vote.
items.exampleCN: 预算表决后政府倒台。

items.example: Governmental agencies share the site.
items.exampleCN: 多个政府机构共用这处场地。

items.example: Governance outlasts governments.
items.exampleCN: 治理比一届届政府更长久。

items.example: The governor called out the guard.
items.exampleCN: 州长调出了国民警卫队。

items.example: The province became ungovernable.
items.exampleCN: 该省变得无法治理。

definition_zh: 立法；立法行为；法律法规（总称）；（某一部）法律
definition_en: the making of laws by an authorized body, or the body of laws so made
core_image: 议事厅里逐条朗读、举手表决，散会后书记员把通过的条文装订成厚册
scene: 辩论持续到深夜，反对党仍要求把每一条都念完再表决。Parliament passed legislation that rewrites the funding formula.
sceneCN: 这里 legislation 指立法机关通过的法律（第 2 个义项：法规总称）；句意为议会通过了一项改写拨款公式的法律。

pos.zh: 立法；立法行为（不可数）
法律法规（不可数，总称）
一部法律（可数，常见于美式用法）

forms.label: 复数（指多部法律，多见于美式用法）

derivatives.zh: 立法（legislation 去后缀构成动词，由产物转指制定过程）
立法的（legislate + -ive「有……性质的」，由动作转指属性）
立法者；议员（legislate + -or「行事者」，由动作转指人）
立法机关（legislate + -ure「机构」，由动作转指机关）

senses.title: The making of laws
senses.definition: the process or act of making laws through an authorized body
senses.definitionCN: 由有权机关制定法律的过程或行为
senses.example: Legislation took eighteen months and three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 立法花了十八个月、经过三个委员会。
senses.why: the Latin noun names the bringing of a law, an act rather than a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本指「把法带来」，是行为而非物品。

senses.title: Laws collectively
senses.definition: the whole body of enacted laws on a subject or in a jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或某一法域已颁行的全部法律
senses.example: Environmental legislation now covers the whole watershed.
senses.exampleCN: 环境法规如今覆盖整个流域。
senses.why: mass-noun use treats statutes as one substance, which is how policy talk usually needs them.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法把诸多法令当作一种物质，政策讨论通常正需要这样。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted law, countable especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 一部已颁行的法律，在美式用法中可数
senses.example: Two legislations were merged into one act.
senses.exampleCN: 两部法令被合并为一项法案。
senses.why: American usage makes the noun countable because each bill becomes a numbered law.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个名词可数化，因为每项议案都会成为一部编号法律。

senses.title: The legislative process
senses.definition: the staged procedure of reading, amending and voting that a bill must pass
senses.definitionCN: 议案必须经过的宣读、修正与表决的分阶段程序
senses.example: The rules of legislation favour whoever controls the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 立法程序偏向掌控议程的一方。
senses.why: procedure is the machinery behind the act, and English uses the same noun for both.
senses.whyCN: 程序是行为背后的机器，英语用同一个名词兼指两者。

senses.title: What a legislature enacts
senses.definition: the output of a parliament or congress, as distinct from rules made by agencies
senses.definitionCN: 议会或国会的产出，区别于行政机关自订的规则
senses.example: Primary legislation needs a vote; guidance does not.
senses.exampleCN: 主要立法需要表决，行政指引则不必。
senses.why: the word marks the source of authority, so it separates parliamentary output from administrative rules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标示权威来源，因此把议会产出与行政规则分开。

senses.title: Delegated legislation
senses.definition: rules made by a minister or agency under powers granted by a statute
senses.definitionCN: 部长或机关依法律授予的权力制定的规则
senses.example: Delegated legislation fills in technical detail the chamber cannot debate.
senses.exampleCN: 次级立法填补议会无法逐条辩论的技术细节。
senses.why: the word travels with the authority to make law, even when that authority has been lent out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随立法权一同转移，即使该权力是被借出去的。

senses.title: Proposed legislation
senses.definition: a bill or draft still before the chamber, spoken of as future law
senses.definitionCN: 仍在议会审议、被视作未来法律的议案或草案
senses.example: Proposed legislation would cap the fee at ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 拟议立法将把这个费用上限设为百分之十。
senses.why: the word is applied ahead of enactment because the shape of the law is already visible in the draft.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在通过之前就被使用，因为法律的形状在草案里已经可见。

senses.title: Rules for an organization
senses.titleCN: 引申：组织内部规则体系
senses.definition: the formal rules by which a body governs its own members or processes
senses.definitionCN: 某机构管理自身成员或流程的成文规则
senses.example: The society's legislation on conflicts of interest is three pages long.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会关于利益冲突的规则有三页纸。
senses.why: private bodies borrow the word when their rules begin to function like statutes.
senses.whyCN: 私人机构在其规则开始像法令一样运作时，便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Legislation comes from Latin legis latio 'a bringing of a law', from lex 'law' and latio 'a bringing', the noun of latus, the past participle of ferre 'to carry'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislation 来自拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」，由 lex「法」与 latio「带来」构成，后者是 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus 的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex meant 'law, statute, a motion put to the people'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为「法、法令、提交民众的动议」。其更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」的旧联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ferre 'to carry, bring' has the suppletive participle latus, from which latio 'a bringing' is formed; the two verbs were already fused in classical usage.
items.cn: ferre「搬运、带来」的过去分词为异干互补的 latus，由其构成 latio「带来」；两者在古典用法中已合并。

items.en: The phrase legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly, a procedural act rather than the text itself.
items.cn: legis latio 这一说法指把议案带到大会之前的程序性行为，而非文本本身。

items.en: Medieval Latin legislatio generalized the phrase into the making of laws by any authorized body.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 legislatio 把这一说法一般化，指任何有权机关制定法律。

items.en: French législation passed into English in the seventeenth century, first as the act and soon after as the body of laws.
items.cn: 法语 législation 在 17 世纪进入英语，先指立法行为，不久也指法律总体。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not precisely dated, and the origin of lex itself remains unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 本身的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the lex or legisl- stem; group two holds words for laws and for the making of them.
note.cn: 第一组共享 lex 或 legisl- 词干；第二组是关于法律与制定法律的词。

entries.definition: Describing a body or power that makes law; it cannot stand for the laws themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 描述制定法律的机关或权力；不能指法律本身。

entries.definition: The assembly that makes law, formed with -ure 'place or body'; a different thing from the laws it makes.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的议会，由 -ure「场所、机构」构成；与其所制定的法律是两回事。

entries.definition: One member who makes law; the noun names a role, not an output.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员之一；指角色，而非产出。

entries.definition: From Latin legitimus 'lawful', built on lex but through a different adjective; it means lawful, not law-making.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legitimus「合法的」，虽出 lex 却经另一形容词；意为合法，而非立法。

entries.definition: A single rule or the whole body of rules; legislation is the making of it or the output as a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 单条规则或全部规则；legislation 指制定过程或作为总体的产出。

entries.definition: A single law passed by a legislature, countable and technical; legislation is the wider mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的单项法律，可数且技术化；legislation 是更宽的总称。

entries.definition: Detailed rules issued by an agency under a statute, usually not requiring a parliamentary vote.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的细则，通常不经议会表决。

entries.definition: A draft law still under consideration; legislation names what it becomes, or the process of making it.
entries.definitionCN: 仍在审议的草案；legislation 指它最终成为的东西，或制定它的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio: the bringing of a law, so the word began as a motion carried forward.
normal.cn: legis latio：把法带来，因此这个词本是一项被送上前的动议。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split act from output: pass legislation, delegated legislation, environmental legislation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出行为与产出：通过立法、授权立法、环境立法。

normal.en: Contrast the pair: a bill is the draft, legislation is the making and the mass of laws.
normal.cn: 对照这一对：bill 是草案，legislation 是制定过程与法律总体。

normal.en: Watch the false friend legitimate: lawful, but built on a different adjective of lex.
normal.cn: 提防假朋友 legitimate：意为合法，却由 lex 的另一形容词构成。

abstract.en: Picture a text carried by hand across a hall before anyone votes on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文本在被人手捧着穿过大厅，之后才有人表决。

abstract.en: Picture shelves that grow a new thick volume every session.
abstract.cn: 想象书架每开一次会就多一本厚册。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that must be read aloud before it can bind anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则必须先被大声读出，才能约束任何人。

examples.en: The state's legislation on groundwater is older than its mapping.
examples.cn: 该州关于地下水的立法比水文测绘还要早。

examples.en: Delegated legislation filled in the standards the chamber left blank.
examples.cn: 次级立法填上了议会留白的技术标准。

examples.en: Industry lobbied against the proposed legislation for two years.
examples.cn: 业界游说反对这项拟议立法达两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lation（带来）＝ 把法带到台面上；记「念一遍、改一遍、举一次手」。

root: 拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」= lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latio「带来」（来自 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a bill from act to archive: making law, the mass of law, one statute, the procedure, parliamentary output, delegated rules, drafts not yet passed, and the rules of a private body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一项议案从行为走到档案：立法、法律总体、单部法律、程序、议会产出、授权规则、尚未通过的草案，以及私人机构的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a text read aloud, amended, voted on, then bound into a thick volume.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文本被朗读、修正、表决，最后装订进厚册。

branches.en: ACT AND MASS: the making of law, then the whole body it accumulates into.
branches.cn: 行为与总体：先制定，再累积成整体。

branches.en: ONE VOLUME: the countable unit inside the mass.
branches.cn: 单册：总体之中的可数单位。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: procedure at work, and the authority that makes its output law.
branches.cn: 机器：程序在运转，以及使其产成为法律的权威。

branches.en: LENT POWER: rule-making handed to ministers and agencies.
branches.cn: 借出的权力：规则制定权交到部长与机关手里。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER THE HALL: drafts spoken of as law, and private bodies drafting their own.
branches.cn: 大厅前后：草案已被当作法律谈论，私人机构也自订规则。

intro.en: Legislation joins a Latin noun for law to a Latin noun for bringing, and the second element still appears in English words of transfer.
intro.cn: legislation 把拉丁语「法」的名词与「带来」的名词接在一起，后一成分仍出现在英语的转移类词中。

latinIntro.en: Lex supplies legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre supply transfer, refer and relate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate。

items.example: Lex is the root of legal and legislate.
items.exampleCN: lex 是 legal 与 legislate 的词根。

items.example: Its participle latus hides inside latio.
items.exampleCN: 其分词 latus 藏在 latio 里。

items.example: Legis latio is the bringing of a bill.
items.exampleCN: legis latio 就是把议案带来。

items.example: The chamber legislates twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 该议会一年立法两次。

items.example: Legislation followed the report by a year.
items.exampleCN: 报告之后一年才有了立法。

items.example: The legislative calendar is short.
items.exampleCN: 立法日程很短。

items.example: The legislator read the amendment aloud.
items.exampleCN: 立法者大声读了修正案。

items.example: The legislature adjourned at midnight.
items.exampleCN: 立法机关午夜休会。

items.example: A legitimate claim differs from a popular one.
items.exampleCN: 合法的诉求与受欢迎的诉求不同。

definition_zh: 立法的；立法机关的；有立法权的；由立法设立的
definition_en: relating to the making of laws or to the body that makes them
core_image: 一间半圆形的议事厅，座位上标着选区名，中央的书记员正在点票
scene: 修稿一直改到表决前一小时，主席仍要求先算清票数。The legislative committee rewrote the clause before the final vote.
sceneCN: 这里 legislative 指属于立法机关及其程序的（第 1 个义项：与立法机关有关）；句意为立法委员会在最终表决前重写了该条款。

pos.zh: 立法的；立法机关的；有立法权的

derivatives.zh: 立法；法规（legislate + -ion「行为或结果」，由属性转指其所指的过程与产物）
立法机关（legislate + -ure「机构」，由属性转指持有它的机关）
立法者（legislate + -or「行事者」，由属性转指人）
立法（由 legislative 的词干逆构，由属性转指行为）

senses.title: Of the law-making body
senses.definition: belonging to the assembly that makes laws, as opposed to the executive or the courts
senses.definitionCN: 属于制定法律的议会，与行政或法院相对
senses.example: The legislative calendar leaves little room for debate.
senses.exampleCN: 立法日程几乎没给辩论留空间。
