senses.why: the suffix -ive marks a body's characteristic function, so the adjective names the branch by what it does.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 标示某机构特有的职能，因此形容词按它做什么来命名这一分支。

senses.title: Holding the power to make law
senses.definition: possessing authority to enact binding law
senses.definitionCN: 持有颁行有约束力法律的权威
senses.example: Legislative power cannot be delegated without limits.
senses.exampleCN: 立法权不能无限制地授出。
senses.why: power is what separates law-making from advising, so the adjective attaches to authority itself.
senses.whyCN: 权力把立法与建议区分开，因此形容词也直接接在权威上。

senses.title: Of the procedure
senses.definition: concerning the steps of reading, amending and voting on a bill
senses.definitionCN: 关于议案的宣读、修正与表决步骤
senses.example: A legislative deadlock can outlast a session.
senses.exampleCN: 立法僵局可以跨会期延续。
senses.why: procedure is the visible part of law-making, so the adjective routinely describes it.
senses.whyCN: 程序是立法最可见的部分，因此形容词经常描述它。

senses.title: Created by statute
senses.definition: established by an act of a legislature rather than by administrative decision
senses.definitionCN: 由立法机关的法令、而非行政决定设立
senses.example: The ombudsman is a legislative creation, not a ministerial one.
senses.exampleCN: 监察专员是立法设立的，而非部长设立的。
senses.why: the adjective can mark origin, telling us which kind of authority brought a body into being.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可标示来源，说明是哪一类权威使某机构得以成立。

senses.title: Law-making in character
senses.definition: having the character of law-making even outside a parliament, as with a treaty clause
senses.definitionCN: 即使不在议会之内，也带立法性质，如条约条款
senses.example: The council's vote had a legislative effect on the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会的投票对整个地区产生了立法效果。
senses.why: the adjective can describe an effect rather than a body, since making binding rules is what defines it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可描述效果而非机构，因为「制定有约束力的规则」才是它的定义特征。

senses.title: Separated from executive and judicial
senses.definition: naming one of the three functions of government in the doctrine of separation of powers
senses.definitionCN: 在三权分立学说中指政府三大职能之一
senses.example: Legislative independence was the point of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 立法独立正是这场改革的要点。
senses.why: the modern sense is defined by contrast: legislative is whatever the other two branches are not.
senses.whyCN: 现代义靠对照定义：立法者就是另外两支所不是的那个。

senses.title: Of members or elections
senses.titleCN: 立法机关成员的、议员选举的
senses.definition: concerning the members of a legislature or the elections that seat them
senses.definitionCN: 关于立法机关成员或使其当选的选举
senses.example: Legislative elections were moved up by six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 立法机关选举提前了六周。
senses.why: metonymy lets the branch stand for the people in it, a very common journalistic shorthand.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让这一分支代表其中的人，是新闻语体极常见的简称。

senses.title: Legislative history
senses.titleCN: 立法沿革资料（用于解释法条）
senses.definition: the record of debates, drafts and reports used by courts to interpret a statute
senses.definitionCN: 法院解释法条时所用的辩论、草案与报告记录
senses.example: Judges read the legislative record before ruling on intent.
senses.exampleCN: 法官在裁定立法意图之前先读立法记录。
senses.why: English gives this technical sense to the adjective because the material belongs to the law-making stage.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个技术义交给形容词，因为该材料属于立法阶段。

intro.en: Legislative is the adjective of legislation, from Latin lex 'law' and latus 'carried', the participle of ferre. The English adjective appears in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislative 是 legislation 的形容词，来自拉丁 lex「法」与 latus「被搬运的」，后者是 ferre 的分词。英语形容词见于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex 'law' has no established deeper origin; the old suggestion of a link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis only.
items.cn: lex「法」的更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」有关的旧说仅为假说。

items.en: Latus is the suppletive participle of ferre 'to carry'; legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly.
items.cn: latus 是 ferre「搬运」的异干互补分词；legis latio 指把议案带到大会之前。

items.en: Legislatio generalized the phrase to law-making, and its adjective legislativus described what belongs to that function.
items.cn: legislatio 把这一说法一般化为立法，其形容词 legislativus 描述属于该职能之物。

items.en: French législatif passed into English in the seventeenth century, at first in writing on the separation of powers.
items.cn: 法语 législatif 在 17 世纪进入英语，最初见于论三权分立的著述。

items.en: With the spread of written constitutions the adjective became a fixed label for one branch, always defined against the executive and the courts.
items.cn: 随着成文宪法的传播，这个形容词成为某一分支的固定标签，总在与行政、法院的对照中被定义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not exactly dated, and the origin of lex remains unsettled, so older forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the legisl- stem; group two holds adjectives of government functions.
note.cn: 第一组共享 legisl- 词干；第二组是政府各职能的形容词。

entries.definition: The act or the body of laws; the adjective only describes what belongs to that act.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或法律总体；形容词只描述属于该行为之物。

entries.definition: The body that legislates; a legislative committee belongs to it rather than being it.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的机构；立法委员会属于它，而不等于它。

entries.definition: From legitimus 'lawful'; it shares the lex root but means permitted, not legislative.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legitimus「合法的」；共享 lex 词根，却意为获准的，而非立法的。

entries.definition: A member who makes law; the adjective would describe the member's work, not the member.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员；形容词描述其工作，而非其本人。

entries.definition: Of a parliament's rules and manners; legislative concerns law-making power, which is narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会的规则与礼仪；legislative 关注立法权，范围更窄。

entries.definition: Created or required by a particular act; legislative describes the function rather than the binding force.
entries.definitionCN: 由某部法令创设或要求；legislative 描述职能，而非约束力。

entries.definition: Of the branch that carries out policy; it is defined by contrast with legislative and judicial.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行政策的分支；它与立法、司法相对而被定义。

entries.definition: The everyday compound for the same idea; legislative is its formal, constitutional counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意思的日常复合词；legislative 是其正式、宪制性的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio 'bringing of a law' plus -ive: having the character of that bringing.
normal.cn: legis latio「把法带来」加 -ive：带有那种「带来」的性质。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branch: legislative power, legislative committee, legislative agenda.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一分支：立法权、立法委员会、立法议程。

normal.en: Three adjectives divide the state: legislative, executive, judicial.
normal.cn: 三个形容词把国家切开：立法的、行政的、司法的。

normal.en: The technical phrase legislative history sends courts back to the debates.
normal.cn: 术语 legislative history 把法院送回辩论记录。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the only thing made is sentences that bind people outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，里面唯一制造的东西是能约束屋外之人的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall that later requires thousands of hands to obey.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里举起的一只手，日后要成千上万只手服从。

abstract.en: Picture three pillars, and the left one is always described by what the other two are not.
abstract.cn: 想象三根柱子，左边那根总是靠另外两根「不是什么」来描述。

examples.en: The legislative branch cannot enforce its own statutes.
examples.cn: 立法分支无法自己执行其法令。

examples.en: A legislative fix would take a full session.
examples.cn: 用立法方式修补需要整整一个会期。

examples.en: The court consulted the legislative record before ruling.
examples.cn: 法院在裁定前查考了立法记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lat（带来）+ ive（……的）＝ 把法带来的那一支；记「只造规则，不管执行」。

root: 拉丁 lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latus「被搬运的」（ferre「搬运」的分词）+ 形容词后缀 -ive。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one function from outside: the body that makes law, the power it holds, its procedure, what it creates, its effect elsewhere, its place in the division of powers, its members, and the record it leaves for courts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从外部描述同一职能：制定法律的机关、它持有的权力、它的程序、它创设之物、它在别处的效果、它在分权中的位置、它的成员，以及它留给法院的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand in a chamber that turns a sentence into a rule binding those outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：议事厅里举起的一只手，把一句话变成约束厅外之人的规则。

branches.en: BODY AND POWER: the assembly, and the authority that makes its words binding.
branches.cn: 机关与权力：议会，以及使其言语有约束力的权威。

branches.en: PROCEDURE AND PRODUCT: the steps, then the bodies and rules those steps create.
branches.cn: 程序与产物：先是步骤，再是这些步骤所创设的机构与规则。

branches.en: EFFECT WITHOUT A CHAMBER: legislative quality can attach to a treaty or a council vote.
branches.cn: 无厅之效：立法性质也可附在条约或委员会表决上。

branches.en: DEFINED BY CONTRAST: the branch is what the executive and the courts are not.
branches.cn: 靠对照定义：这一分支就是行政与法院所不是的。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PAPER: the members elected, and the record they leave behind.
branches.cn: 人与纸：选出的成员，以及他们留下的记录。

intro.en: Legislative is built from a Latin law noun, a Latin participle and an English adjective suffix, so each part can be read alone.
intro.cn: legislative 由拉丁「法」名词、拉丁分词与英语形容词后缀构成，每一部分都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Lex gives legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre give transfer, refer, relate and translate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate、translate。

items.example: Lex underlies legal and legitimate.
items.exampleCN: lex 支撑 legal 与 legitimate。

items.example: The participle supplies the second half of legislation.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了 legislation 的后半。

items.meaning: tending to, having the character of
items.example: The suffix turns a function into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一种职能变成形容词。

items.example: Only the chamber may legislate here.
items.exampleCN: 此处只有该院可以立法。

items.example: The legislative session opened late.
items.exampleCN: 立法会期开得晚。

items.example: Legislation followed the inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 调查之后才有立法。

items.example: The legislature met for six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 立法机关开了六周会。

items.example: The issue was addressed legislatively.
items.exampleCN: 该问题是以立法方式处理的。

items.example: One legislator held the floor for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 一位议员占了一个小时的发言。

definition_zh: 法律（总称）；一条法律；定律；规则；执法机构；法学
definition_en: a rule that a community accepts as binding, or the whole system of such rules, or a regular pattern in nature
core_image: 石柱上刻着一排条文，旁边站着执法的人，远处实验室的黑板上写着另一条「定律」
scene: 公告栏上钉着新条文，摊主们围着读，谁也没先开口。The new law reaches every stall in the market.
sceneCN: 这里 law 指正式颁行的一条法律（第 2 个义项：一部法律）；句意为这条新法律管到市场上的每一个摊位。

pos.zh: 法律；法规（不可数，总称）
一条法律；法令（可数）
定律；法则
（口语，用定冠词）执法机构；警方

derivatives.zh: 合法的（law + -ful「充满」，由法律转指符合其要求）
无法无天的（law + -less「无」，由法律转指其缺失）
律师（law + -yer「从事者」，由法律转指以此为业的人）
亡命之徒；宣布非法（out「在外」+ law，由法律转指被逐出法外）

senses.title: The system of rules
senses.definition: the whole body of binding rules of a community, seen as one system
senses.definitionCN: 某一社群全部有约束力的规则，被视为一个体系
senses.example: Law is slow, but it remembers.
senses.exampleCN: 法律很慢，但它记得住。
senses.why: the mass-noun use is the oldest general sense: law as an institution rather than a list of items.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法是最古老的泛指义：法作为制度，而非条目清单。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted rule with a number, a date and an issuing body
senses.definitionCN: 带编号、日期与颁行机关的单条规则
senses.example: The new law reaches every stall in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新法律管到市场上的每一个摊位。
senses.why: English made law countable so that individual acts could be cited and dated.
senses.whyCN: 英语让 law 可数，以便单条法令可被引用与记年。

senses.title: A regularity of nature
senses.definition: a statement that a natural process always behaves in a specified way
senses.definitionCN: 断言某一自然过程总以特定方式进行的陈述
senses.example: The law holds far from the laboratory as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这条定律在实验室之外也成立。
senses.why: the seventeenth century extended the word from decrees to regularities, since both are rules that cannot be broken.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪把这个词从法令扩展到规律，因为两者都是不可违反的规则。

senses.title: A rule of a game or body
senses.titleCN: 比赛或机构内部的规则
senses.definition: an agreed rule governing play, a society or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 约定管辖比赛、社团或机构的规则
senses.example: The law of the club is older than the clubhouse.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部的规则比会所还老。
senses.why: any self-governing body reproduces the statute model, so the word follows the rule wherever it binds.
senses.whyCN: 任何自治团体都会复制法令的模式，于是这个词跟着规则走到哪里绑到哪里。

senses.title: The police, in speech
senses.definition: the police or the enforcement arm, used with the definite article
senses.definitionCN: 警察或执法部门，惯用定冠词
senses.example: The law arrived twenty minutes after the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 警笛响过二十分钟后警察就到了。
senses.why: metonymy names the enforcers by the thing they enforce, an old colloquial habit.
senses.whyCN: 转喻用所执行之物来称呼执行者，是古老的口语习惯。

senses.title: The study and profession
senses.definition: the academic discipline of law and the profession that practises it
senses.definitionCN: 研究法律的学科以及以此执业的行业
senses.example: She read law before joining the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她入部之前读的是法律。
senses.why: a body of rules large enough to need specialists becomes a discipline and a career.
senses.whyCN: 规则多到需要专家时，便成为一门学科与一种职业。

senses.title: A governing principle
senses.definition: a principle that explains how a domain works, as in the law of supply and demand
senses.definitionCN: 解释某一领域如何运作的原理，如供需法则
senses.example: The law of supply and demand explains the queue, not the price.
senses.exampleCN: 供需法则解释的是排队，不是价格。
senses.why: economics borrowed the prestige of natural law to describe tendencies that hold on average.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借来自然法的威望，用来描述平均成立的趋势。

senses.title: An inescapable rule
senses.definition: a rule presented as unavoidable, as in the law of the jungle
senses.definitionCN: 被说成不可避免的规则，如丛林法则
senses.example: The law of the jungle returned when the patrols stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻一停，丛林法则就回来了。
senses.why: the figurative use keeps the binding force and drops the institution, leaving only inevitability.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法保留了约束力而丢掉机构，只剩不可避免。

intro.en: Law comes from Old English lagu, itself borrowed from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', from leggja 'to lay'. It has no Latin source, unlike legal and legislation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: law 来自古英语 lagu，而 lagu 借自古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」，出自 leggja「放置」。与 legal、legislation 不同，它没有拉丁来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lag meant 'something laid down, a layer, a fixed order', from the verb leggja 'to lay'. The image is a rule placed down where people can see it.
items.cn: lag 意为「被放下之物、层次、既定秩序」，出自动词 leggja「放置」。意象是被放在人们看得见之处的规则。

items.en: Old English borrowed lagu from Norse during the Viking period; the native word for divine law was ǣ, which later dropped out.
items.cn: 古英语在维京时期从诺斯语借入 lagu；本土表示神法的词是 ǣ，后来消失。

items.en: Lagu settled into Middle English as lawe, taking over the general sense of binding custom and statute.
items.cn: lagu 进入中古英语作 lawe，接管了有约束力的习俗与法令这一泛义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century law was applied to regularities of nature, so that a falling apple and a statute shared one word.
items.cn: 17 世纪起 law 被用于自然规律，于是落下的苹果与一条法令共用同一个词。

items.en: Legal, legitimate and legislation descend from Latin lex, not from lagu; the resemblance is in meaning only, and the two families are unrelated at the root.
items.cn: legal、legitimate、legislation 上溯拉丁 lex，而非 lagu；相似只在意义上，两个词族在词根上并无关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Norse origin of lag is not established, and the relation sometimes proposed between lag and the English verb lay is plausible but not demonstrated as a direct derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：lag 在诺斯语之前的来源未得到证明；有人提出 lag 与英语动词 lay 的关系，看似合理，却未被证明为直接派生。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look related to law but come from Latin lex; group two holds near neighbours in the legal field.
note.cn: 第一组是看着与 law 有关、实际来自拉丁 lex 的词；第二组是法律领域的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin legalis, built on lex; it means permitted by law, not the law itself, and is unrelated at the root to law.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legalis，由 lex 构成；意为法律允许的，而非法律本身，与 law 在词根上无关。

entries.definition: The making of laws, from lex and latus; it names the process, not the Norse-rooted body of rules.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律，来自 lex 与 latus；指过程，而非那个诺斯语词根的规则总体。

entries.definition: law plus -ful: conforming to the rules, an adjective built on the native noun.
entries.definitionCN: law 加 -ful：符合规则的，是本族名词派生的形容词。

entries.definition: Out 'outside' plus law: one placed outside the law's protection, so the root is kept and reversed.
entries.definitionCN: out「在外」加 law：被置于法律保护之外的人，词根保留而意义反转。

entries.definition: A formal written law passed by a legislature; law is the wider word that also covers custom and case law.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的正式成文法；law 是更宽的说法，也涵盖习惯法与判例法。

entries.definition: A regulation of an activity or a game; law implies a community's binding authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 某项活动或比赛的规章；law 暗含社群约束性权威在其背后。

entries.definition: A rule issued by an agency under a statute; it is law in a derived, technical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的规则；在派生、技术的意义上也是法。

entries.definition: A general truth that explains workings; it matches the scientific sense of law without any authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 解释运作的一般真理；对应 law 的科学义，背后却没有权威。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old Norse lag 'something laid down': a rule is a thing placed where all can see it.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」：规则就是放在人人看得见之处的东西。

normal.en: The family runs lawful, lawless, lawyer, outlaw, by-law.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lawful、lawless、lawyer、outlaw、by-law。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: break the law, by law, the rule of law, a law of nature.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出义项：违法、依法、法治、自然定律。

normal.en: Two senses share one word: the statute in the book and the regularity on the blackboard.
normal.cn: 两个义项共用一个词：书里的法令与黑板上的规律。

normal.en: Keep legal apart: it comes from Latin lex, so its resemblance to law is meaning, not blood.
normal.cn: 把 legal 分开放：它来自拉丁 lex，与 law 的相似是意义上的，不是血缘上的。

abstract.en: Picture a stone with lines cut into it, standing where everyone walks past.
abstract.cn: 想象一块刻着横线的石头，立在人人都经过的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that keeps working after the person who wrote it is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则，写它的人不在了，它还在运作。

abstract.en: Picture two blackboards, one with a statute, one with an equation, both called law.
abstract.cn: 想象两块黑板，一块写着法令，一块写着方程，都叫 law。

examples.en: The law requires the seller to name the origin of the goods.
examples.cn: 法律要求卖方标明货物的产地。

examples.en: By law, the minutes must be public within a month.
examples.cn: 依法，会议记录必须在一个月内公开。

examples.en: The law of demand fails when buyers cannot compare prices.
examples.cn: 当买方无法比较价格时，需求法则就失效。

dict_mnemonic.text: law＝「放下的东西」：一条条放在那里、谁都得照着走；记「书里有条文，黑板上有定律」。

root: 古英语 lagu ← 古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」← leggja「放置」；lag 在诺斯语之前的来源不确定，与英语 lay 的关系仅为合理推测。与拉丁 lex 词族（legal、legislation）无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one laid-down rule: the system, a single act, a regularity of nature, a game rule, the police, the profession, an economic principle, and an unavoidable rule of the jungle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一条被放下的规则散开：体系、单条法令、自然规律、比赛规则、警方、法律职业、经济原理，以及丛林里的必然规矩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rule laid down in public, heavy enough that people arrange their days around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条当众放下的规则，重到人们要围着它安排日子。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND UNIT: the whole body of rules, then one dated item inside it.
branches.cn: 体系与单位：规则总体，以及其中一条记年的条目。

branches.en: RULES WITHOUT A LAWGIVER: nature and the market exhibit regularities that cannot be disobeyed.
branches.cn: 没有立法者的规则：自然与市场呈现不可违背的规律。

branches.en: SMALL SCALES OF BINDING: a club's rulebook, and the jungle's unavoidable order.
branches.cn: 约束的小尺度：俱乐部的规则手册，以及丛林的必然秩序。

branches.en: THE ENFORCERS: the police named by what they enforce.
branches.cn: 执行者：用所执行之物来称呼警察。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: a body of rules large enough to become a career.
branches.cn: 学科：规则多到足以成为一种职业。

intro.en: Law is a Norse loanword, so its family is built with English suffixes rather than Latin ones, unlike legal and legislation.
intro.cn: law 是诺斯语借词，因此其词族由英语后缀而非拉丁后缀构成，这一点与 legal、legislation 不同。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin entry here: the Latin lex family supplies legal and legislation but is not related to law at the root.
latinIntro.cn: 此处没有拉丁条目：拉丁 lex 词族给出 legal 与 legislation，但与 law 在词根上无关。

items.meaning: a binding rule; the body of such rules
items.meaningCN: 有约束力的规则；此类规则的总体
items.example: The law was read from the steps.
items.exampleCN: 法律从台阶上被宣读。

items.example: The search was lawful but rude.
items.exampleCN: 这次搜查合法，却失礼。

items.example: The port grew lawless after the garrison left.
items.exampleCN: 驻军撤走后港口变得无法无天。

items.example: Her lawyer read the clause twice.
items.exampleCN: 她的律师把条款读了两遍。

items.meaning: one put outside the law; to ban
items.meaningCN: 被置于法外者；宣布非法
items.example: The practice was outlawed in the last session.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法在上个会期被宣布非法。

items.example: The by-law limits noise after ten.
items.exampleCN: 该细则限制十点后的噪音。

items.example: Lawmakers argued over the wording.
items.exampleCN: 立法者就措辞争论。

items.example: The legality of the order was disputed.
items.exampleCN: 这道命令的合法性受到质疑。

definition_zh: 司法系统；司法权；法官群体；司法机构
definition_en: the branch of government that interprets and applies the law, or the judges of a country taken as a body
core_image: 一排高背椅，台上放着天平与卷宗，台下两个人站着等候裁断
scene: 庭上先核对卷宗页码，再让双方各说十分钟，最后才落槌。An independent judiciary can overturn a minister's order.
sceneCN: 这里 judiciary 指独立行使裁判权的司法系统（第 1 个义项：作为司法分支）；句意为独立的司法系统可以推翻部长的命令。

pos.zh: 司法系统；司法分支（通常用单数，带定冠词）
法官群体；司法人员

collocations.zh: 安插亲信进入司法系统

derivatives.zh: 司法的（judiciary 去后缀，由机构转指其属性）
法官；判断（拉丁 iudex「宣法者」，由人转指其行为）
判决；判断（judge + -ment「结果」，由行为转指结果）
明智的（拉丁 iudicium + -ous，由裁断转指判断力好）

senses.title: The judicial branch
senses.definition: the branch of government that decides cases and interprets the law
senses.definitionCN: 裁定案件并解释法律的政府分支
senses.example: The judiciary is the third branch, not the first.
senses.exampleCN: 司法是第三分支，不是第一分支。
senses.why: the noun in -ary names the whole body of courts as one institution.
senses.whyCN: -ary 结尾的名词把全部法院当作一个机构来命名。

senses.title: Judges as a body
senses.definition: the judges of a jurisdiction considered collectively, with their shared training and tenure
senses.definitionCN: 某一法域的法官作为整体，共享训练与任期保障
senses.example: The judiciary met in private before the term opened.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭期之前法官们私下聚了一次。
senses.why: the same noun shifts from the institution to the people who staff it, a standard metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从机构转指在其中任职的人，是常见的转喻。

senses.title: Judicial power
senses.definition: the authority to adjudicate disputes and to declare what the law requires
senses.definitionCN: 裁断争议并宣示法律要求的权威
senses.example: Judicial power includes the right to say what a statute means.
senses.exampleCN: 司法权包含解释法令含义的权力。
senses.why: an institution is also a power, and constitutional writing often needs the abstract noun.
senses.whyCN: 机构同时也是一种权力，宪制文本常需要这个抽象名词。

senses.title: The courts as institutions
senses.definition: the system of courts, their staffs, budgets and administrative machinery
senses.definitionCN: 法院体系及其人员、预算与行政机器
senses.example: The judiciary's budget was cut for the third year.
senses.exampleCN: 司法系统的预算连续第三年被削减。
senses.why: administration makes the branch visible as an employer and a spender, not only as a decider.
senses.whyCN: 行政管理让这一分支显形为雇主与支出者，而不只是裁断者。

senses.title: Independence as a value
senses.definition: the quality of deciding without instruction from ministers or parties
senses.definitionCN: 不受部长或党派指示而裁断的品质
senses.example: An independent judiciary can overturn a minister's order.
senses.exampleCN: 独立的司法系统可以推翻部长的命令。
senses.why: the word carries the value of independence because that is what separates judging from command.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着独立的价值观，因为正是独立把裁断与命令分开。

senses.title: A country's judicial branch
senses.definition: the concrete national system, named in constitutions and comparative studies
senses.definitionCN: 被宪法与比较研究所指称的具体国别体系
senses.example: The two judiciaries differ in how judges are chosen.
senses.exampleCN: 两套司法系统在法官选任方式上不同。
senses.why: comparison requires a countable unit, so the noun takes a plural for national systems.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要可数单位，于是这个名词用复数指各国体系。

senses.title: Adjudicative function in general
senses.definition: the function of deciding disputes according to pre-existing rules, whoever performs it
senses.definitionCN: 依既定规则裁断争议的职能，无论由谁执行
senses.example: International tribunals borrow the judiciary's method without its tenure.
senses.exampleCN: 国际法庭借用了司法的裁断方法，却没有其任期保障。
senses.why: the defining activity can be detached from the state, leaving a general function.
senses.whyCN: 定义性的活动可从国家剥离，留下一个一般职能。

senses.title: Disciplinary panels elsewhere
senses.titleCN: 引申：其他领域的裁判机构
senses.definition: a body that hears and decides disputes inside a sport, a profession or a union
senses.definitionCN: 在体育、行业或工会内部听审并裁定争议的机构
senses.example: The sport's judiciary banned two riders for a season.
senses.exampleCN: 该运动的裁判机构对两名骑手禁赛一季。
senses.why: any body that hears both sides and rules on a record reproduces the court's shape.
senses.whyCN: 任何听双方陈述、依记录裁定的机构都复制了法庭的形状。

intro.en: Judiciary comes from Latin iudiciarius 'of a judge', from iudicium 'judgment', from iudex 'judge', itself from ius 'law, right' and dicere 'to say'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: judiciary 来自拉丁 iudiciarius「法官的」，上溯 iudicium「裁断」，再上溯 iudex「法官」，后者由 ius「法、权利」与 dicere「说」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ius meant 'law, right, what is due'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to iurare 'to swear' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: ius 意为「法、权利、应得之物」。其更深来源未得到证明；与 iurare「发誓」的旧联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Dicere 'to say, declare' supplied the second half; iudex is literally one who declares the law.
items.cn: dicere「说、宣告」提供后半；iudex 字面就是宣告法律的人。

items.en: Iudicium meant 'judgment, trial, the court', and iudiciarius described whatever belonged to a judge or a trial.
items.cn: iudicium 意为「裁断、审判、法庭」，iudiciarius 描述属于法官或审判之物。

items.en: Medieval Latin extended iudiciarius to the office and the body of judges, the sense English would borrow.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁把 iudiciarius 扩展到职位与法官群体，这正是英语借用的义项。

items.en: English took judiciary in the seventeenth century for the courts as a branch, and later for judges as a class.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 judiciary，指作为分支的法院体系，后又指法官阶层。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of ius remains unsettled, so forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；ius 在拉丁语之前的来源仍无定论，为其提出的形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the iudex stem; group two holds words for courts and for judging.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iudex 词干；第二组是关于法院与裁断的词。

entries.definition: Of courts or judges; it describes a decision or a process, while judiciary names the body itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指法院或法官的；描述决定或程序，而 judiciary 指机构本身。

entries.definition: From iudicium plus -ous: showing good judgement, a personal quality rather than an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 由 iudicium 加 -ous：显出良好判断力，属个人品质而非机构。

entries.definition: One who decides cases; through French the Latin iudex lost its medial consonant and became this short word.
entries.definitionCN: 裁定案件的人；经法语，拉丁 iudex 掉了中间辅音，成为这个短词。

entries.definition: Ad- 'to' plus iudicare: to hear and decide a dispute, the verb behind the noun's activity.
entries.definitionCN: ad-「向」加 iudicare：听审并裁定争议，是名词所指活动的动词。

entries.definition: A single tribunal or its building; the judiciary is the whole set of them as a branch.
entries.definitionCN: 单个法庭或其建筑；judiciary 是作为分支的全部法院。

entries.definition: Metonym for judges sitting together, used in news and legal writing; narrower than judiciary.
entries.definitionCN: 指同坐审案的法官，用于新闻与法律写作；比 judiciary 窄。

entries.definition: The body of magistrates, a lower tier within a judiciary rather than the whole branch.
entries.definitionCN: 治安法官群体，是司法系统内的较低层级，而非整个分支。

entries.definition: A body set up to decide a particular class of dispute; it may sit outside the ordinary judiciary.
entries.definitionCN: 为裁定某类争议而设的机构；可能设在普通司法系统之外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ius 'law' + dicere 'to say': a judge is one who says what the law is.
normal.cn: ius「法」+ dicere「说」：法官就是说出法律是什么的人。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judicial, judiciary, judicious, adjudicate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judicial、judiciary、judicious、adjudicate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branch: an independent judiciary, the federal judiciary, judiciary committee.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一分支：独立司法、联邦司法系统、司法委员会。

normal.en: The plural counts systems: two judiciaries, two ways of choosing judges.
normal.cn: 复数用来数体系：两套司法系统，两种法官选任方式。

normal.en: Keep judicious apart: it means sensible, not judicial.
normal.cn: 把 judicious 分开放：它指明智，不指司法。

abstract.en: Picture a chair higher than the room, so that whoever sits there must look down to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一把比房间还高的椅子，坐上去的人必须向下看才能说话。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that keeps weighing after the argument has ended.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，争论结束后还在称。

abstract.en: Picture a record book that can overrule the person who wrote the order.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记录册能推翻写下命令的那个人。

examples.en: The judiciary refused to comment on the pending case.
examples.cn: 司法系统拒绝评论待审案件。

examples.en: Reformers wanted the judiciary chosen by an independent panel.
examples.cn: 改革者希望司法人员由独立的小组选任。

examples.en: The sport's judiciary heard the appeal in private.
examples.cn: 该运动的裁判机构私下审理了上诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: jud（法）+ iciary（机构）＝ 说法的那套机构；记「高椅、天平、卷宗」。

root: 拉丁 iudiciarius「法官的」← iudicium「裁断」← iudex「法官」= ius「法、权利」（更深来源不确定，与 iurare「发誓」的联系仅为假说）+ dicere「说、宣告」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bench: the branch, the judges on it, the power they hold, their administration, their independence, one country's version, the function detached from the state, and panels that copy the shape elsewhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一张法官席展开：分支、席上的法官、他们持有的权力、其行政、其独立、某国的版本、从国家剥离的职能，以及别处复制这一形状的裁判机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised bench, a scale, a file of pages, and two parties waiting for one sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：高起的法官席、一架天平、一叠卷宗，以及等待一句话的双方。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: a single national system, then several systems compared.
branches.cn: 一与多：单个国别体系，再到数套体系作比较。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: the judges whose training and tenure define the body.
branches.cn: 人：以训练与任期界定这一机构的法官们。

branches.en: THE POWER: the authority to say what the law requires.
branches.cn: 权力：宣示法律要求什么的权威。

branches.en: BUDGET AND BACKBONE: courts as employers, and the independence that keeps them courts.
branches.cn: 预算与脊梁：法院作为雇主，以及使其仍为法院的独立。

branches.en: DETACHED SHAPE: the adjudicative function, then panels in sport and trade that reuse it.
branches.cn: 剥离的形状：裁判职能本身，再到体育与行业中复用它的小组。

intro.en: Judiciary is a Latin adjective turned noun, built from ius, dicere and the suffix -arius, so its parts still appear across English.
intro.cn: judiciary 是由拉丁形容词转成的名词，由 ius、dicere 与后缀 -arius 构成，各部分仍散布在英语中。

latinIntro.en: Ius and iudex give judge, judgment, judicial, judicious and adjudicate; dicere also gives dictate, verdict and predict.
latinIntro.cn: ius 与 iudex 衍生 judge、judgment、judicial、judicious、adjudicate；dicere 还衍生 dictate、verdict、predict。

items.example: Ius is the first half of iudex.
items.exampleCN: ius 是 iudex 的前半。

items.structure: dicere, dixi, dictum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: A judge declares what the law is.
items.exampleCN: 法官宣告法律是什么。

items.example: The iudex heard both sides.
items.exampleCN: 法官听了双方陈述。

items.example: Iudicium also gives judicious.
items.exampleCN: iudicium 还给出 judicious。

items.meaning: of a judge or a court
items.example: The adjective became the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词变成了英语名词。

items.example: The judge read the ruling aloud.
items.exampleCN: 法官大声读了裁定。

items.example: Judicial review is a separate power.
items.exampleCN: 司法审查是一项单独的权能。

items.example: A judicious silence saved the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 一次明智的沉默救了那场会。

items.example: A panel adjudicates the claims.
items.exampleCN: 一个小组裁定这些主张。

definition_zh: 司法的；法院的；法官的；审判上的；审慎公正的
definition_en: relating to courts, judges or the deciding of cases, and sometimes meaning carefully fair
core_image: 一份裁定书首页盖着法院的印章，正文第一句就写明「本院认为」
scene: 裁定书送到时，双方都先翻到最后一页看结论，再回头看理由。The judicial review found the order unlawful.
sceneCN: 这里 judicial 指属于法院审查程序的（第 3 个义项：司法审查的）；句意为司法审查认定该命令不合法。

pos.zh: 司法的；法院的；审判的
审慎公正的（多见于 judicial temperament 一类说法）

derivatives.zh: 司法系统（judicial + -ary「机构」，由属性转指持有它的机关）
以司法方式（judicial + -ly，由属性转指方式）
明智的（与 judicial 同出 iudicium，但走的是「判断力」一路）
有害的；有偏见的（prae-「在前」+ iudicium，由「预先裁断」转指不利影响）

senses.title: Of the courts
senses.definition: belonging to the court system as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为机构的法院体系
senses.example: The judicial system handles ten thousand claims a year.
senses.exampleCN: 司法系统每年处理一万件请求。
senses.why: the Latin adjective meant 'of a judge', and English widened it to the whole court apparatus.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词本指「法官的」，英语把它扩到整个法院机器。

senses.title: Of a judge's work
senses.definition: concerning the act of hearing and deciding a case
senses.definitionCN: 关于听审并裁定案件的行为
senses.example: Judicial discretion is narrow where the rule is clear.
senses.exampleCN: 规则清楚之处，法官的裁量空间很小。
senses.why: the core sense stays with the person who declares the law, not with the building.
senses.whyCN: 核心义仍系于宣告法律的那个人，而非建筑。

senses.title: Judicial review
senses.definition: concerning a court's power to strike down acts of other branches
senses.definitionCN: 关于法院推翻其他分支行为的权力
senses.example: The judicial review found the order unlawful.
senses.exampleCN: 司法审查认定该命令不合法。
senses.why: review makes the adjective name a specific power rather than a general quality.
senses.whyCN: 「审查」这一搭配使这个形容词指一项具体权力，而非一般性质。

senses.title: Of a ruling
senses.definition: issued by a court in the form of a binding decision
senses.definitionCN: 由法院以有约束力的决定形式发出
senses.example: A judicial order stopped the eviction for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 一项司法命令把驱逐推迟了一个月。
senses.why: once issued, a decision carries the authority of the bench that made it.
senses.whyCN: 一经发出，决定便带上作出它的法官席的权威。

senses.title: Fair and deliberate
senses.definition: showing the calm, even-handed manner expected of a judge
senses.definitionCN: 显出法官应有的沉着与不偏不倚
senses.example: She answered with a judicial calm that annoyed the questioner.
senses.exampleCN: 她以司法者般的沉着作答，反倒惹恼了提问者。
senses.why: the manner of judging became a personal virtue, so the adjective can describe a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 裁断的作风成了一种个人德性，因此形容词可描述性情。

senses.title: By court order
senses.titleCN: 由法院裁定的、司法裁定的
senses.definition: imposed or authorized by a court rather than by an agency
senses.definitionCN: 由法院而非行政机关施加或授权
senses.example: The records were released under judicial compulsion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些记录是在司法强制下公布的。
senses.why: the adjective marks the source of authority, separating court orders from administrative ones.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标示权威来源，把法院命令与行政命令分开。

senses.title: One of three functions
senses.definition: naming the third function of government in the doctrine of separation of powers
senses.definitionCN: 在三权分立学说中指政府的第三项职能
senses.example: Judicial independence is written into the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 司法独立被写入宪法。
senses.why: constitutional language needs three parallel adjectives, and this one is defined by contrast.
senses.whyCN: 宪制语言需要三个并列形容词，这一个靠对照定义。

senses.title: Of procedure
senses.definition: concerning the steps by which a dispute is heard and decided
senses.definitionCN: 关于听审并裁定争议所经的步骤
senses.example: Judicial delay hurts claimants more than defendants.
senses.exampleCN: 司法拖延对索赔者的伤害大于对被告。
senses.why: procedure is the observable face of judging, so the adjective attaches to it naturally.
senses.whyCN: 程序是裁断可见的那一面，因此形容词自然附上去。

intro.en: Judicial comes from Latin iudicialis, from iudicium 'judgment', from iudex 'judge', built on ius 'law, right' and dicere 'to say'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: judicial 来自拉丁 iudicialis，上溯 iudicium「裁断」，再上溯 iudex「法官」，由 ius「法、权利」与 dicere「说」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ius 'law, right' has no established deeper origin; the suggestion of a link to iurare 'to swear' remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: ius「法、权利」的更深来源未得到证明；与 iurare「发誓」有关的说法仍属假说。

items.en: Ius plus dicere produced iudex, literally one who declares what is lawful, and iudicium, the declaring itself.
items.cn: ius 加 dicere 构成 iudex，字面即宣告何为合法者，以及 iudicium，即这一宣告本身。

items.en: Iudicialis meant 'of a judge or a trial', the adjective of iudicium, and it passed through French into English.
items.cn: iudicialis 意为「法官的、审判的」，是 iudicium 的形容词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: English took judicial in the sixteenth century, first for the deciding of cases and soon for the whole court system.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 judicial，先指案件的裁断，不久也指整个法院体系。

items.en: Judicious, built on the same iudicium but with -ous, kept the sense of good judgement, while judicial kept the institutional sense.
items.cn: judicious 同出 iudicium 但带 -ous，保留「判断力好」之义；judicial 则保留机构义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not exactly dated, and the origin of ius is unsettled, so older forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；ius 的来源无定论，为其提出的更早形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the iudicium stem; group two holds near neighbours in legal description.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iudicium 词干；第二组是法律描述上的近义词。

entries.definition: The courts or judges as an institution; judicial describes what belongs to them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为机构的法院或法官；judicial 描述属于它们之物。

entries.definition: Sensible and prudent, a quality of decisions; it is not a synonym of judicial despite the shared stem.
entries.definitionCN: 明智审慎，是决定的品质；虽共享词干，却非 judicial 的同义词。

entries.definition: Of courts and judges; the pair judicial and judicious is one of the commonest confusions in legal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 指法院与法官的；judicial 与 judicious 是法律文字中最常见的混淆之一。

entries.definition: From Latin iuridicus, ius plus dicere again, but through a different adjective; it means relating to law as a system.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 iuridicus，仍是 ius 加 dicere，却经另一形容词；意为与法律体系有关的。

entries.definition: Concerning law as a body of rules, including statutes and contracts; judicial is narrower and points at courts.
entries.definitionCN: 关于作为规则总体的法律，含法令与合同；judicial 更窄，指向法院。

entries.definition: Used before a noun for what belongs to a tribunal, as in a court order; judicial is the formal equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 置于名词前指属于法庭之物，如法院命令；judicial 是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: Of the process of hearing and ruling; judicial also covers the institution, not only the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指听审与裁定的过程；judicial 还涵盖机构，不限于行为。

entries.definition: Of evidence and argument in court; it is technical and evidential where judicial is institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 指法庭上的证据与论证；偏技术与证据，而 judicial 偏机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ius 'law' + dicere 'say': judicial work is saying what the law already requires.
normal.cn: ius「法」+ dicere「说」：司法工作就是说出法律已经要求的东西。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the power: judicial review, judicial power, judicial independence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出权力：司法审查、司法权、司法独立。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judiciary, judicial, judicious, prejudicial, adjudicate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judiciary、judicial、judicious、prejudicial、adjudicate。

normal.en: Keep the pair apart: judicial is the bench, judicious is the good sense behind a decision.
normal.cn: 把这一对分开：judicial 是法官席，judicious 是决定背后的明智。

normal.en: Judicially is the adverb: the claim was judicially resolved.
normal.cn: 副词是 judicially：该请求经司法途径解决。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp that turns an opinion into something the whole country must obey.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章，把一段意见变成全国都得服从的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a judge who speaks last, after everyone else has spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一位最后发言的法官，别人都说完他才开口。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that must be visibly level, or the room stops trusting it.
abstract.cn: 想象一架必须让人看见它平的天平，否则整个房间就不再信它。

examples.en: The judicial branch cannot write its own budget.
examples.cn: 司法分支无法自己写预算。

examples.en: A judicial inquiry cleared the officer but criticized the practice.
examples.cn: 一项司法调查洗清了这位警官，却批评了那套做法。

examples.en: Judicial appointments became the centre of the debate.
examples.cn: 司法任命成了辩论的中心。

dict_mnemonic.text: jud（法）+ icial（……的）＝ 与法官席有关的；记「法院盖章，judicious 是脑子清楚」。

root: 拉丁 iudicialis ← iudicium「裁断」← iudex「法官」= ius「法、权利」（更深来源不确定）+ dicere「说、宣告」；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle one bench: the court system, a judge at work, review of other branches, a binding order, a fair manner, a court-authorized act, the third function of government, and the procedure that carries it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围着一张法官席：法院体系、法官在工作、审查其他分支、有约束力的命令、公正作风、经法院授权的行为、政府第三项职能，以及承载它的程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruling sheet stamped with a court seal, beginning with the words the court holds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份盖着法院印章的裁定书，开头写着「本院认为」。

branches.en: BUILDING AND BENCH: the institution, then the person deciding inside it.
branches.cn: 楼与席：先是机构，再是在其中裁断的人。

branches.en: POWER AND ITS INSTRUMENT: review, then the order that carries the result.
branches.cn: 权力与其工具：审查，以及承载结果的命令。

branches.en: MANNER AS VIRTUE: the judge's calm becomes an admired personal quality.
branches.cn: 作风成德：法官的沉着变成一种被赞赏的个人品质。

branches.en: SOURCE OF AUTHORITY: court-authorized, as against administrative.
branches.cn: 权威来源：法院授权，与行政相对。

branches.en: THE THIRD FUNCTION AND ITS STEPS: one constitutional branch, and the procedure that makes it visible.
branches.cn: 第三职能与步骤：一个宪制分支，以及使它可见的程序。

intro.en: Judicial is a Latin adjective in -alis built on a noun of judging, and both parts recur throughout legal English.
intro.cn: judicial 是 -alis 结尾的拉丁形容词，建立在表示裁断的名词上，两部分在法律英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Iudicium gives judicial, judicious and prejudice; iudex gives judge and judgment; dicere gives verdict, predict and dictate.
latinIntro.cn: iudicium 衍生 judicial、judicious、prejudice；iudex 衍生 judge、judgment；dicere 衍生 verdict、predict、dictate。

items.example: Ius also gives jurist and jury.
items.exampleCN: ius 还给出 jurist 与 jury。

items.example: Dicere gives verdict and predict.
items.exampleCN: dicere 给出 verdict 与 predict。

items.example: The iudex spoke after both parties.
items.exampleCN: 法官在双方之后发言。

items.example: Iudicium is the base of judicial.
items.exampleCN: iudicium 是 judicial 的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns a trial into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把审判变成形容词。

items.example: Judicial notice is a narrow doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 司法认知是一项范围很窄的学说。

items.example: A judicious cut saved the budget.
items.exampleCN: 一次明智的削减救了预算。

items.example: Delay was prejudicial to the defence.
items.exampleCN: 拖延对辩方不利。

items.example: The judiciary answers to no minister.
items.exampleCN: 司法系统不对任何部长负责。

latinEntries.meaning: of a judge or a trial

definition_zh: 社会阶层；社会等级；阶级（社会学概念）
definition_en: a group of people ranked together by income, occupation, education and standing, or the system of such rankings
core_image: 同一栋楼里，不同楼层的人用不同的电梯，孩子们上不同的学校
scene: 同一条街的两端，信箱里的信件来自不同的学校与不同的诊所。Social class shaped who survived the epidemic and who was merely ill.
sceneCN: 这里 social class 指与阶层位置相关的结果差异（第 5 个义项：与阶层相关的结果差异）；句意为社会阶层决定了谁能熬过这场疫病，谁只是生病。

pos.zh: 社会阶层；社会等级（可数，指某一阶层；不可数，指分层现象）

derivatives.zh: 等级；类别（拉丁 classis「民众的划分」，由划分转指类别本身）
分类（class + -ify「使成为」，由类别转指归类的动作）
无阶层的（class + -less「无」，由阶层转指其缺失）
使社会化；交际（social + -ize，由社会关系转指使之进入关系）

senses.title: The system of ranks
senses.definition: the whole arrangement by which a society ranks its members in tiers
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会把成员分成层级的整套安排
senses.example: Social class is inherited more often than it is chosen.
senses.exampleCN: 社会阶层多半是继承的，而非选择的。
senses.why: the compound names a structure rather than one rung, so it is used for the system itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组命名的是结构而非一级阶梯，因此用于体系本身。

senses.title: One tier of people
senses.definition: a group sharing roughly similar income, occupation and education
senses.definitionCN: 收入、职业与教育大致相近的一群人
senses.example: The town had three social classes and one road.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇子有三个阶层和一条路。
senses.why: counting tiers requires a countable noun, and the compound supplies one.
senses.whyCN: 要数层级，就需要可数名词，这个词组正好提供。

senses.title: The criteria of rank
senses.definition: the measures, such as income, schooling or occupation, used to place people
senses.definitionCN: 用来给人定位的尺度，如收入、学历或职业
senses.example: Social class in that survey meant income and schooling only.
senses.exampleCN: 在那份调查里，社会阶层只指收入与学历。
senses.why: every ranking needs a yardstick, and the phrase can name the yardstick instead of the result.
senses.whyCN: 任何排序都需要尺子，这个词组可以指尺子而非结果。

senses.title: Class identity
senses.definition: the sense of belonging to a tier and of sharing its interests
senses.definitionCN: 对某一层级的归属感与共享利益之感
senses.example: Social class became visible when the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关门时，社会阶层就显形了。
senses.why: a rank becomes a social fact when people act on it, so the phrase also names awareness.
senses.whyCN: 当人们据此行动时，等级就成了社会事实，因此这个词组也指意识。

senses.title: Class-linked outcomes
senses.titleCN: 与阶层相关的差异结果
senses.definition: differences in health, schooling and life expectancy that follow rank
senses.definitionCN: 随等级出现的健康、学业与寿命差异
senses.example: Social class predicts the diagnosis more accurately than the postcode.
senses.exampleCN: 社会阶层比邮编更能预测诊断结果。
senses.why: researchers needed a term for the pattern, not for the persons, and this is it.
senses.whyCN: 研究者需要一个词指这个模式而非人，这个词组正是。

senses.title: Mobility between tiers
senses.definition: movement upward or downward between classes across a lifetime or generations
senses.definitionCN: 一生或数代之间在阶层间的上下移动
senses.example: Social class still limits how far a scholarship can carry a student.
senses.exampleCN: 社会阶层仍限制着奖学金能把学生送多远。
senses.why: mobility is measured against class, so the phrase names the frame that movement crosses.
senses.whyCN: 流动是相对阶层来衡量的，因此这个词组命名被穿越的那个框架。

senses.title: Upper, middle, lower
senses.definition: the familiar three-tier vocabulary used in everyday description
senses.definitionCN: 日常描述中常见的三层说法
senses.example: The labels upper, middle and lower still organize social class in speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 上层、中层、下层这些标签仍组织着演讲里的社会阶层。
senses.why: the phrase carries the inherited three-tier scheme even when data do not fit it.
senses.whyCN: 即使数据不合，这个词组仍带着继承下来的三层图式。

senses.title: An analytic category
senses.definition: a variable used in sociological models to explain inequality
senses.definitionCN: 社会学模型中用来解释不平等的变量
senses.example: The paper treats social class as a variable, not a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文把社会阶层当作一个变量，而不是判决。
senses.why: the analytic sense deliberately strips the phrase of moral tone so it can be measured.
senses.whyCN: 分析义刻意剥去道德语气，以便它可以被测量。

intro.en: Social class joins social, from Latin socius 'companion', to class, from Latin classis 'a division of the Roman people'. The compound is a modern coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social class 把 social 与 class 接在一起：social 来自拉丁 socius「同伴」，class 来自拉丁 classis「罗马民众的划分单位」。整个词组是近代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally', from a root for following; socialis 'of a companion or an alliance' produced social.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、同盟者」，其词根含「跟随」之意；socialis「同伴的、结盟的」产生 social。

items.en: Classis named a division of the Roman people for voting and military service, and also a fleet. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: classis 指罗马民众按投票与兵役所分的等级，也指舰队。其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: English class first meant a group of students, then a category, and only later a social rank.
items.cn: 英语 class 先指一批学生，再指类别，最后才指社会等级。

items.en: Social entered English through French in the sixteenth century, meaning 'of society or of companions'.
items.cn: social 在 16 世纪经法语进入英语，意为「社会的、同伴的」。

items.en: Social class became a fixed phrase in nineteenth-century writing on industrial society, when rank ceased to be fixed by birth alone.
items.cn: social class 在 19 世纪论工业社会的著述中成为固定说法，当时等级不再只由出身决定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first use of the exact phrase is not precisely dated, and the origin of classis is unsettled, so forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切词组的首用没有精确年代；classis 的来源亦无定论，为其提出的形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one gathers words built on class or close in form; group two holds terms for social ranking.
note.cn: 第一组是以 class 构成或形近的词；第二组是社会分层的术语。

entries.definition: A category, a school group or a rank; social class specifies the rank in a whole society.
entries.definitionCN: 类别、班级或等级；social class 限定为整个社会中的等级。

entries.definition: From Latin classicus 'of the highest class of citizens', a derivative of classis; it means exemplary, not social rank.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 classicus「最高等级公民的」，是 classis 的派生；意为典范的，而非社会等级。

entries.definition: To sort into categories; it shares the class stem but says nothing about hierarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 按类别分开；共享 class 词干，却不涉及等级。

entries.definition: Of society or interaction, from socius; alone it carries no rank.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会或交往的，来自 socius；单独使用不含等级义。

entries.definition: A hereditary rank closed to outsiders, as in the Indian system; social class is usually open in principle.
entries.definitionCN: 由出身决定、对外封闭的等级，如印度制度；social class 原则上通常可流动。

entries.definition: A composite index of income, education and occupation; it is the quantitative cousin of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 收入、教育与职业的合成指数；是这一词组的定量表亲。

entries.definition: A single layer in a ranked society, used in sociology for one tier rather than the system.
entries.definitionCN: 分层社会中的单层，社会学用来指一级而非体系。

entries.definition: A person's position as judged by others; it is individual where social class is collective.
entries.definitionCN: 他人所评定的个人位置；属个人，而 social class 属群体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: classis was a division of the Roman people, so class began as a slice of a population.
normal.cn: classis 是罗马民众的划分单位，因此 class 本是一块人口切片。

normal.en: socius 'companion' + -alis: social means of companions, and class adds the ranking.
normal.cn: socius「同伴」+ -alis：social 指同伴之间的，class 再加上等级。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: working-class background, class divide, social mobility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：工人阶级出身、阶层鸿沟、社会流动。

normal.en: The family runs class, classify, classic, classless, social, socialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 class、classify、classic、classless、social、socialize。

normal.en: Compare the trio: class is the short word, social class the society-wide rank, caste the closed version.
normal.cn: 比较三个：class 是短词，social class 是全社会的等级，caste 是封闭版。

abstract.en: Picture a building where the lift buttons are labelled by income.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼，电梯按钮按收入标注。

abstract.en: Picture two children born a street apart and never in the same classroom.
abstract.cn: 想象两个相差一条街出生的孩子，从未同班。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose rungs are visible only when someone climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，只有有人攀爬时横档才显形。

examples.en: Social class still decides which school a child can reach.
examples.cn: 社会阶层仍决定一个孩子能上哪所学校。

examples.en: The study found social class mattered more than the hospital.
examples.cn: 研究发现社会阶层比医院更重要。

examples.en: He wrote about social class without ever naming his own.
examples.cn: 他写社会阶层，却从不提自己属于哪一层。

dict_mnemonic.text: social（社会的）+ class（等级）＝ 社会里的那几级台阶；记「同一条街，不同的学校」。

root: social：拉丁 socius「同伴」+ -alis「……的」；class：拉丁 classis「罗马民众的划分单位」，其更深来源不确定；整个词组为 19 世纪固定说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses go from structure to measurement: the ranking system, one tier, the yardstick, the sense of belonging, the outcomes that follow rank, movement across ranks, the everyday three-tier labels, and the sociologist's variable.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从结构走到测量：分层体系、某一层级、划分尺度、归属意识、随等级而来的结果、跨层流动、日常的三层标签，以及社会学家的变量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one street whose two ends send their children to different schools and their sick to different clinics.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条街的两端，孩子上不同的学校，病人去不同的诊所。

branches.en: FRAME AND LABELS: the whole ranking, then the familiar upper-middle-lower shorthand.
branches.cn: 框架与标签：先是整套排序，再是上中下的日常简称。

branches.en: UNIT AND RULER: one tier of people, and the measures that put them there.
branches.cn: 单位与尺子：一层人，以及把他们放上去的尺度。

branches.en: THE INSIDE VIEW: rank becomes real when people feel they belong to it.
branches.cn: 内部视角：当人们感到自己属于某一层，等级才成真。

branches.en: CAUSE AND ESCAPE: outcomes follow rank, and mobility is the attempt to leave it.
branches.cn: 因果与逃逸：结果随等级而来，流动则是试图离开它。

branches.en: THE VARIABLE: analysis turns the phrase into something measurable.
branches.cn: 变量：分析把这一词组变成可测量之物。

intro.en: Social class is a two-word phrase: social is a Latin adjective from socius, class a Latin noun from classis, and each half builds its own family.
intro.cn: social class 是两词短语：social 是由 socius 来的拉丁形容词，class 是由 classis 来的拉丁名词，两半各有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Socius gives social, society, associate and sociable; classis gives class, classic and classify.
latinIntro.cn: socius 衍生 social、society、associate、sociable；classis 衍生 class、classic、classify。

items.example: Socius is the base of social.
items.exampleCN: socius 是 social 的基础。

items.example: Socialis passed through French as social.
items.exampleCN: socialis 经法语成为 social。

items.meaning: a division of the people; a fleet
items.example: Classis named a voting division.
items.exampleCN: classis 指一个投票单位。

items.example: The word narrowed from divisions to ranks.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从划分收窄为等级。

items.example: A classic is a work of the first rank.
items.exampleCN: classic 指第一流的作品。

items.example: They classify the records by decade.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年代给记录分类。

items.example: Social ties cross class lines unevenly.
items.exampleCN: 社会关系跨越阶层线并不均匀。

items.meaning: to mix socially; to make social
items.example: Children socialize across the divide.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们跨过那道鸿沟交往。

definition_zh: 贵族阶层；贵族统治；精英上层；（文化上的）精英集团
definition_en: a class of people holding inherited privilege and rank, or government by such a class
core_image: 一座带家族纹章的老宅，客厅里挂着几代人的肖像，来访者要先递上名帖
scene: 老宅的门房先看名帖上的姓氏，再决定去哪间客厅通报。The old aristocracy kept its land through every change of regime.
sceneCN: 这里 aristocracy 指世袭拥有土地与地位的贵族阶层（第 1 个义项：作为阶层群体）；句意为这个古老的贵族阶层历经每次政权更替都保住了土地。

pos.zh: 贵族阶层（可数，指某一国的贵族；不可数，指该阶层整体）
贵族统治；精英统治

derivatives.zh: 贵族（aristocracy 去后缀，由阶层转指其中一员）
贵族的（aristocrat + -ic，由人转指其属性）
专制（auto-「自身」+ -cracy，同后缀而异词根）
财阀统治（ploutos「财富」+ -cracy，由财富转指掌权者）

senses.title: The hereditary class
senses.definition: the families who hold inherited title, land or privilege and pass it on
senses.definitionCN: 世袭持有头衔、土地或特权并传给后代的家族
senses.example: The old aristocracy kept its land through every change of regime.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老的贵族阶层历经每次政权更替都保住了土地。
senses.why: the Greek compound named rule by the 'best', and the class that claimed to be best became the word's centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊复合词本指「最优者」的统治，自称最优的那个阶层随后成了词的中心。

senses.title: Government by nobles
senses.definition: a constitutional form in which a small hereditary class holds political power
senses.definitionCN: 由少数世袭阶层掌握政治权力的政体形式
senses.example: Aristocracy was defended as a check on the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 贵族政治曾被辩护为对人群的制衡。
senses.why: the political sense is the original one, preserved in the -cracy ending.
senses.whyCN: 政治义是原本的义项，保存在 -cracy 后缀里。

senses.title: Rule by the best, in theory
senses.definition: the classical claim that the most capable should rule, whether or not by birth
senses.definitionCN: 古典主张：最有能力者应当统治，不论是否出于出身
senses.example: Aristocracy in theory need not be hereditary at all.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上的最优者统治根本不必是世袭的。
senses.why: aristos meant 'best', not 'well born', and philosophers kept that distinction alive.
senses.whyCN: aristos 意为「最优」，不是「出身好」，哲学家一直保留这一区分。

senses.title: Any privileged upper group
senses.titleCN: 任何一个特权上层集团
senses.definition: an advantaged group that closes ranks and reproduces its advantages
senses.definitionCN: 抱团并复制自身优势的有利群体
senses.example: The party became an aristocracy of its own founding families.
senses.exampleCN: 这个党变成了由创始家族构成的贵族层。
senses.why: the word travels to any group that behaves like a hereditary elite, even without titles.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有头衔，任何行为像世袭精英的群体也能被这个词覆盖。

senses.title: The privileges themselves
senses.definition: the exemptions, offices and advantages reserved for the class
senses.definitionCN: 专为该阶层保留的豁免、职位与好处
senses.example: Tax exemptions were the aristocracy's most durable privilege.
senses.exampleCN: 免税是贵族最持久的特权。
senses.why: metonymy lets the class stand for what it holds, and privileges were what it held.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让阶层代表它所持有之物，而它持有的正是特权。

senses.title: A country's nobles collectively
senses.definition: the noble families of one country taken as a single body
senses.definitionCN: 一国贵族家族被视为一个整体
senses.example: The English aristocracy married into trade for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 英国贵族与商界通婚长达两个世纪。
senses.why: national histories need one noun for the whole body, and this is the usual one.
senses.whyCN: 国别史需要一个词指整体，这通常就是那个词。

senses.title: A cultural elite
senses.definition: a group that dominates taste and standards without holding office
senses.definitionCN: 不掌权却主导品味与标准的群体
senses.example: Critics spoke of an aristocracy of taste.
senses.exampleCN: 批评家谈到一种品味上的贵族。
senses.why: authority over standards reproduces the old claim to be the best, minus the land.
senses.whyCN: 对标准的话语权复制了旧的「最优」主张，只是没有了土地。

senses.title: An entrenched elite
senses.definition: a closed circle that defends its position against newcomers
senses.definitionCN: 对外来者守门、维护自身地位的封闭圈子
senses.example: The university was called an aristocracy of examiners.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学被称作考官构成的贵族集团。
senses.why: the pejorative use keeps only the closure, which is what critics object to.
senses.whyCN: 贬义用法只留下封闭性，而批评者反对的正是封闭。

intro.en: Aristocracy comes from Greek aristokratia 'rule of the best', built on aristos 'best' and kratos 'power'. It entered English through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aristocracy 来自希腊 aristokratia「最优者的统治」，由 aristos「最优」与 kratos「力量」构成。它经法语在 16 世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aristos meant 'best' and served as the superlative of agathos 'good'. Its formation is not fully explained; the older segmentation into a prefix and an unknown root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: aristos 意为「最优」，是 agathos「好」的最高级。其构成未获完整解释；把它切成前缀加未知词根的旧办法只是假说。

items.en: Kratos meant 'strength, might', and -kratia named a form of rule, as in democracy and oligarchy.
items.cn: kratos 意为「力量、强权」，-kratia 指某种统治形式，如民主制与寡头制。

items.en: Aristokratia named rule by the best citizens, a constitutional form discussed by Plato and Aristotle rather than a hereditary class.
items.cn: aristokratia 指最优公民的统治，是柏拉图与亚里士多德讨论的一种政体，而非世袭阶层。

items.en: French aristocratie passed the political term into English in the sixteenth century, still meaning a form of government.
items.cn: 法语 aristocratie 在 16 世纪把这个政治术语带入英语，当时仍指一种政体。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word commonly named the noble class itself, especially after that class lost direct rule.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，这个词常指贵族阶层本身，尤其在该阶层失去直接统治权之后。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the internal make-up of aristos is not established, and the pre-Greek origin of kratos is unsettled, so older forms offered for either are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：aristos 的内部构成未得到证明；kratos 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，为二者提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the -cracy or arist- stem; group two holds terms for ruling classes.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -cracy 或 arist- 词干；第二组是统治阶层的术语。

entries.definition: A single member of the class; aristocracy names the class or the form of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 该阶层的一员；aristocracy 指阶层或统治形式。

entries.definition: Describing noble origin or manner; it cannot stand for the class itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述贵族出身或风度；不能指阶层本身。

entries.definition: Autos 'self' plus kratos: rule by one person alone, sharing the suffix but not the claim to be best.
entries.definitionCN: autos「自身」加 kratos：一人独治，后缀相同，却没有「最优」的主张。

entries.definition: Rule by those judged most able, often coined as the opposite of inherited aristocracy.
entries.definitionCN: 由被认为最有能力者统治，常被造出来作为世袭贵族制的对立面。

entries.definition: The body of titled families, close to the first sense of aristocracy but without the claim about rule.
entries.definitionCN: 有头衔的家族总体，接近 aristocracy 的第一义，但不含统治主张。

entries.definition: The minor landed class below the nobility, especially in England; aristocracy can include them loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 贵族之下有地而无头衔的阶层，尤指英格兰；aristocracy 有时宽泛地包含他们。

entries.tag: few rulers, no claim of best
entries.definition: Rule by a small group, defined by number rather than by virtue; aristocracy claims virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 由小集团统治，按人数而非德性定义；aristocracy 则自称德性。

entries.definition: The most advantaged group in any field; it is neutral about birth, which aristocracy is not.
entries.definitionCN: 任一领域中最占优势的群体；对出身中性，aristocracy 则不然。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aristos 'best' + kratos 'power': the best claiming the power.
normal.cn: aristos「最优」+ kratos「权力」：最优者主张权力。

normal.en: The family runs aristocrat, aristocracy, aristocratic, and the rival meritocracy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aristocrat、aristocracy、aristocratic，以及对手词 meritocracy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the class: the landed aristocracy, the old aristocracy, aristocracy of wealth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶层：有地贵族、旧贵族、财富贵族。

normal.en: Keep the suffix in view: democracy, autocracy, oligarchy, plutocracy all share -cracy.
normal.cn: 留意后缀：democracy、autocracy、oligarchy、plutocracy 都共享 -cracy。

normal.en: The Greek sense was a constitution, not a family tree; the class meaning came later.
normal.cn: 希腊义是一种政体，不是家谱；阶层义是后来才有的。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only to certain surnames.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，只对某些姓氏打开。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait gallery where every face resembles the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一间肖像廊，每张脸都像上一张。

abstract.en: Picture a claim to be best that nobody has to prove at the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一种「我们最优」的主张，在门口无需任何人证明。

examples.en: The landed aristocracy opposed the new inheritance tax.
examples.cn: 拥有土地的贵族反对新的遗产税。

examples.en: He argued that an aristocracy of talent is still an aristocracy.
examples.cn: 他主张，才能贵族仍然是一种贵族。

examples.en: Aristocracy survived the revolution better than the monarchy did.
examples.cn: 贵族阶层比君主制更经得住那场革命。

dict_mnemonic.text: aristo（最优）+ cracy（统治）＝ 自称最优者的统治；记「姓氏、土地、名帖」。

root: 希腊 aristokratia「最优者的统治」= aristos「最优」（其构成未获完整解释）+ kratos「力量」（希腊语之前的来源属重构形式）；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a constitution to a closed circle: the hereditary class, noble rule, the theoretical rule of the best, any privileged upper group, its privileges, one country's nobles, a cultural elite, and an entrenched circle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一种政体走到一个封闭圈子：世袭阶层、贵族统治、理论上的最优者统治、任何特权上层、其特权、一国贵族整体、文化精英，以及盘踞的圈子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house whose gatekeeper reads surnames before deciding which room to announce you to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座宅子，门房先看姓氏，再决定把你通报到哪间屋。

branches.en: THEORY AND OFFICE: rule by the best as a constitution, then as a philosophical claim.
branches.cn: 理论与职位：作为政体的最优者统治，再作为哲学主张。

branches.en: CLASS AND COUNTRY: one hereditary body, then a whole nation's nobles.
branches.cn: 阶层与国别：一个世袭群体，再是一国的全部贵族。

branches.en: THE SHAPE TRAVELS: any group that closes ranks can be called aristocratic.
branches.cn: 形状在迁移：任何抱团的群体都可被称作贵族式。

branches.en: WHAT IT HOLDS: privileges are what the class actually possesses.
branches.cn: 它持有什么：特权才是这个阶层实际握有的东西。

branches.en: WITHOUT LAND: taste and gatekeeping reproduce the claim in other fields.
branches.cn: 没有土地之后：品味与守门在其他领域复制了这一主张。

intro.en: Aristocracy joins a Greek superlative to a Greek noun of power, and both halves recur in English political words.
intro.cn: aristocracy 把希腊语最高级与希腊语「力量」名词接在一起，两半都反复出现在英语政治词中。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements reached English through Latin and French; kratos supplies -cracy, and aristos survives only in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊成分经拉丁语与法语进入英语；kratos 提供 -cracy，aristos 只存于这个词族。

items.example: Aristos names the best, not the well born.
items.exampleCN: aristos 指最优，而非出身好。

items.example: Kratos is the second half of many constitutions.
items.exampleCN: kratos 是许多政体词的后半。

items.example: Democracy and autocracy share this suffix.
items.exampleCN: democracy 与 autocracy 共享这个后缀。

items.meaning: a member of a ruling group
items.example: An aristocrat claims the first rank.
items.exampleCN: 贵族主张第一等的位置。

items.meaning: rule of the best; their class
items.example: Aristocracy then meant a constitution.
items.exampleCN: aristocracy 当时指一种政体。

items.meaning: a member of the noble class
items.example: The aristocrat refused the new title.
items.exampleCN: 那位贵族拒绝了新封号。

items.example: An aristocratic accent travels further than money.
items.exampleCN: 贵族口音比钱走得更远。

items.example: Meritocracy was coined against aristocracy.
items.exampleCN: meritocracy 是为对抗 aristocracy 而造的。

definition_zh: 贵族的；贵族出身的；贵族式的；高傲的
definition_en: belonging to or characteristic of a noble class, especially in manner, taste or bearing
core_image: 一个年轻人站在老宅的石阶上，背挺得很直，说话很慢，却从不动手做事
scene: 来人宁可站着等半小时，也不肯自己去搬那把椅子。He had an aristocratic dislike of anything that looked like effort.
sceneCN: 这里 aristocratic 指贵族式的、带着阶层习气与傲气的（第 2 个义项：贵族式的风度）；句意为他对一切看上去像出力的东西都有一种贵族式的厌恶。

pos.zh: 贵族的；贵族出身的；贵族式的

derivatives.zh: 贵族阶层（aristocratic 去后缀，由属性转指持有它的阶层）
贵族（aristocracy + -crat「成员」，由阶层转指其中一员）
以贵族方式（aristocratic + -ally，由属性转指方式）
贵族作风（少见派生，aristocratic + -ism，由属性转指作风体系）

senses.title: Of noble birth
senses.definition: born into a family holding inherited title, land or rank
senses.definitionCN: 出生于世袭持有头衔、土地或等级的家族
senses.example: Her aristocratic origins opened doors that money could not.
senses.exampleCN: 她的贵族出身打开了钱打不开的门。
senses.why: the adjective attaches the class to a person, and birth is the oldest marker of that class.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把阶层接到人身上，而出身是这一阶层最古老的标记。

senses.title: In noble manner
senses.definition: carrying oneself with the reserve and assurance associated with the class
senses.definitionCN: 带着与该阶层相关的克制与笃定行事
senses.example: He had an aristocratic dislike of anything that looked like effort.
senses.exampleCN: 他对一切看上去像出力的东西都有一种贵族式的厌恶。
senses.why: manner outlives title, so the adjective often describes bearing rather than a pedigree.
senses.whyCN: 风度比头衔活得久，因此形容词常描述举止而非家谱。

senses.title: Of noble rule
senses.definition: concerning government by a hereditary elite
senses.definitionCN: 关于由世袭精英统治
senses.example: The aristocratic constitution gave the upper chamber a veto.
senses.exampleCN: 贵族政制给上院一票否决权。
senses.why: the political sense survives in constitutional history, where forms rather than families are at issue.
senses.whyCN: 政治义存于宪制史中，那里讨论的是形式而非家族。

senses.title: Haughty
senses.definition: showing a superior air that expects deference
senses.definitionCN: 显出期待他人退让的优越姿态
senses.example: His aristocratic shrug ended the conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个贵族式的耸肩结束了谈话。
senses.why: the manner becomes a vice when the assurance turns into contempt.
senses.whyCN: 当笃定转为轻蔑，风度就成了一种毛病。

senses.title: Of noble taste
senses.definition: showing the cultivated preferences historically cultivated by the class
senses.definitionCN: 显出历史上由该阶层培养出的偏好
senses.example: The collection reflects aristocratic taste in furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 这批藏品反映了贵族在家具上的品味。
senses.why: leisure and inheritance produced a style that later spreads far beyond the class.
senses.whyCN: 闲暇与继承造就一种风格，这种风格后来远播阶层之外。

senses.title: Of an upper social layer
senses.definition: belonging to the top layer of a local society, titled or not
senses.definitionCN: 属于某地社会的顶层，无论有无头衔
senses.example: The town's aristocratic set met on the same veranda each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的上流圈子每年夏天都在同一个游廊聚会。
senses.why: in small places the class is defined socially rather than legally, and the adjective follows.
senses.whyCN: 在小地方，阶层由社交而非法律界定，形容词也随之。

senses.title: Exclusive in spirit
senses.definition: reserved for a closed circle and cold to outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 只对封闭圈子开放，对外人冷淡
senses.example: The club kept an aristocratic membership rule for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 该俱乐部维持了一个世纪的排他入会规则。
senses.why: exclusiveness is the social mechanism that keeps the class a class.
senses.whyCN: 排他性是使这一阶层成其为阶层的社交机制。

senses.title: Of a cultural elite
senses.titleCN: 文化精英的、精英主义的
senses.definition: marking a claim to superior standards in art or letters, without any title
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术或文学上主张更高标准，却无任何头衔
senses.example: The journal's aristocratic tone kept younger writers out.
senses.exampleCN: 这份刊物的精英腔调把年轻作者挡在门外。
senses.why: the word can describe anyone who borrows the class's authority over standards.
senses.whyCN: 任何借用该阶层对标准之权威的人，都能被这个词描述。

intro.en: Aristocratic is aristocracy plus -ic, from Greek aristos 'best' and kratos 'power', passed through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aristocratic 是 aristocracy 加 -ic，来自希腊 aristos「最优」与 kratos「力量」，经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aristos 'best' was the superlative of agathos; its internal formation is not fully explained and older segmentations are hypotheses.
items.cn: aristos「最优」是 agathos 的最高级；其内部构成未获完整解释，较早的切分办法均属假说。

items.en: Aristokratia named a constitution in which the best citizens ruled, a term of political theory before it named a class.
items.cn: aristokratia 指最优公民统治的政体，在指阶层之前是政治理论的术语。

items.en: French supplied the adjective, and English took it in the eighteenth century as noble families became a social rather than a ruling body.
items.cn: 法语提供形容词，英语在 18 世纪借入，正值贵族家族成为社会群体而非统治机构。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the adjective spread from birth to bearing, taste and disdain, describing a style anyone might imitate.
items.cn: 19 世纪这个形容词从出身扩展到举止、品味与轻蔑，描述一种人人可模仿的风格。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English use of the adjective is not precisely dated, and neither the make-up of aristos nor the pre-Greek origin of kratos is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：形容词的最早英语用法没有确切年代；aristos 的构成与 kratos 在希腊语之前的来源均未得到证明。

note.en: Group one shares the arist- stem; group two holds adjectives of class and bearing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 arist- 词干；第二组是关于阶层与风度的形容词。

entries.definition: The class or the form of rule; the adjective describes a person or manner belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 阶层或统治形式；形容词描述属于它的人或风度。

entries.definition: One member of the class; the adjective could describe that member's bearing but not the member.
entries.definitionCN: 该阶层的一员；形容词可描述其风度，却不能指其人。

entries.definition: Of one-person rule, sharing -cratic but not the claim to be best.
entries.definitionCN: 指一人统治，共享 -cratic，却没有「最优」的主张。

entries.definition: Of rule by tested ability; it is often set against aristocratic as birth against merit.
entries.definitionCN: 指由被考核的能力统治；常与 aristocratic 对立，即出身对才能。

entries.definition: Of titled rank, or morally elevated; aristocratic stresses the class and its habits rather than virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 有头衔的，或品格高尚的；aristocratic 强调阶层及其习气，而非德性。

entries.definition: Of the hereditary upper class, originally the Roman senatorial families; narrower and more historical.
entries.definitionCN: 指世袭上层，原指罗马元老家族；更窄也更历史化。

entries.definition: Refined and respectable, often with a hint of pretending; it concerns manners only.
entries.definitionCN: 文雅体面，常带一点装样；只涉及举止。

entries.definition: The everyday compound for the top social layer; aristocratic adds heritage and style.
entries.definitionCN: 顶层社会的日常说法；aristocratic 另加世系与风格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aristos 'best' + -cratic 'ruling': originally about who should rule, later about who was born where.
normal.cn: aristos「最优」+ -cratic「统治的」：原问谁该统治，后来问谁生在哪里。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark manner more than birth: aristocratic bearing, aristocratic disdain, aristocratic taste.
normal.cn: 固定搭配更多标出风度而非出身：贵族气度、贵族式轻蔑、贵族品味。

normal.en: The family runs aristocracy, aristocrat, aristocratic, aristocratically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aristocracy、aristocrat、aristocratic、aristocratically。

normal.en: It pairs with its opposite: aristocratic birth against meritocratic examination.
normal.cn: 它与反义词配对：贵族出身对精英考试。

normal.en: The adverb names the manner: he refused aristocratically.
normal.cn: 副词指方式：他以贵族式的方式拒绝了。

abstract.en: Picture a straight back that has never once carried a chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一副挺直的背，从未搬过一把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a slow voice that makes other people speed up.
abstract.cn: 想象一个缓慢的声音，让别人都快了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a door that is polite to everyone and open to almost no one.
abstract.cn: 想象一道对人人客气、却几乎不对任何人打开的门。

examples.en: The family kept an aristocratic reserve even after the estate was sold.
examples.cn: 庄园卖掉之后，这家人仍保持着贵族式的矜持。

examples.en: His aristocratic accent survived four years of factory work.
examples.cn: 四年的工厂生活也没磨掉他的贵族口音。

examples.en: Critics detected an aristocratic bias in the reading list.
examples.cn: 批评者在书单里看出一种贵族式的偏斜。

dict_mnemonic.text: aristo（最优）+ cratic（统治的）＝ 自认最优那一层的；记「背直、语慢、不搬椅」。

root: 希腊 aristos「最优」（其构成未获完整解释）+ kratos「力量」（希腊语之前的来源属重构形式）+ 形容词后缀 -ic；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from pedigree to posture: noble birth, noble bearing, noble rule, haughtiness, cultivated taste, the local upper set, exclusiveness, and a cultural claim to better standards.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从家谱走到姿态：贵族出身、贵族风度、贵族统治、高傲、有教养的品味、地方上层圈子、排他性，以及文化上主张更高标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing very straight on a stone step, speaking slowly, lifting nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人笔直站在石阶上，说话很慢，什么也不搬。

branches.en: BIRTH AND OFFICE: the pedigree, then the constitution built on it.
branches.cn: 出身与职位：先是家谱，再是建立在它之上的政体。

branches.en: THE BODY SPEAKS: manner survives after title loses its power.
branches.cn: 身体在说话：头衔失权之后，风度仍在。

branches.en: THE VICE OF THE VIRTUE: assurance curdles into contempt.
branches.cn: 德性的毛病：笃定凝成了轻蔑。

branches.en: TASTE AND NEIGHBOURHOOD: cultivated style, and the local top set that shares it.
branches.cn: 品味与邻里：有教养的风格，以及共享它的地方上层。

branches.en: CLOSURE: the membership rule, and the cultural gate kept on standards.
branches.cn: 封闭：入会规则，以及以标准为名守着的文化之门。

intro.en: Aristocratic combines a Greek superlative, a Greek noun of power and an English adjective suffix; only the last is not Greek in origin.
intro.cn: aristocratic 合并希腊语最高级、希腊语「力量」名词与英语形容词后缀；只有最后一项不出希腊语。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements reached English through Latin and French; kratos yields -cratic, and aristos appears nowhere else in English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊成分经拉丁语与法语进入英语；kratos 给出 -cratic，aristos 在英语中不见于他处。

items.example: The word once meant best, not best born.
items.exampleCN: 这个词本指最优，而非出身最优。

items.example: Kratos supplies the -cracy family.
items.exampleCN: kratos 提供 -cracy 词族。

items.meaning: of a named form of rule
items.example: Democratic and autocratic share this ending.
items.exampleCN: democratic 与 autocratic 共享这一词尾。

items.meaning: rule of the best; their class
items.example: Aristocracy began as a constitution.
items.exampleCN: aristocracy 起初是一种政体。

items.example: The aristocrat sold the portrait quietly.
items.exampleCN: 那位贵族悄悄卖掉了肖像。

items.example: Aristocratic manners travel light.
items.exampleCN: 贵族风度不需行李。

items.example: She nodded aristocratically.
items.exampleCN: 她以贵族式的方式点了点头。

items.example: Meritocratic tests replaced aristocratic connections.
items.exampleCN: 精英考试取代了贵族人脉。

definition_zh: 艺术；美术；技艺；技巧；人文学科；狡诈
definition_en: the making of things meant to be looked at or heard for their own quality, or the skill that such making requires
core_image: 画室里颜料未干，画布旁边的调色板上留着上一笔的痕迹，墙上挂着一把旧刻刀
scene: 画室里颜料还没干，作者把画笔搁在罐沿上，退后两步看整幅画。The gallery hung the art so low that visitors had to stoop.
sceneCN: 这里 art 指供人观看的美术作品（第 3 个义项：美术作品）；句意为画廊把作品挂得太低，参观者都得弯腰。

pos.zh: 艺术；美术（不可数，指门类或活动）
技艺；技巧（可数，常用于「……的艺术」这一结构）
人文学科（复数形式）
（古）狡诈；计谋

derivatives.zh: 艺术家（art + -ist「从事者」，由门类转指从事者）
艺术的（artist + -ic，由人转指其属性）
巧妙的；狡猾的（art + -ful「充满」，由技艺转指手段多）
朴拙的；不做作的（art + -less「无」，由技巧转指其缺失）

senses.title: Art as an activity
senses.definition: the making of works valued for form, expression or beauty rather than use
senses.definitionCN: 制作因形式、表达或美而受重视、而非因实用受重视的作品
senses.example: Art asks for attention, not agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术要求的是注意，不是同意。
senses.why: the mass-noun sense names a whole field of human activity, the sense most used today.
senses.whyCN: 不可数义命名一整片人类活动领域，是今天最常用的义项。

senses.title: A skill or craft
senses.definition: a practised skill in doing something well, as in the art of negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 把某事做好的熟练本领，如谈判的艺术
senses.example: Grafting is an art learned slowly in the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 嫁接是在果园里慢慢学会的一门技艺。
senses.why: this is the oldest English sense: art as trained skill, before it meant fine art.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最古老的义项：艺术指训练有素的技能，早于「美术」。

senses.title: Works made to be seen
senses.definition: paintings, drawings and sculptures considered as objects
senses.definitionCN: 作为物件的绘画、素描与雕塑
senses.example: The auction house insured the art for more than the building.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖行为这批作品投保的金额超过了那栋楼。
senses.why: the shift from skill to object happened in the eighteenth century, when works began to be collected as art.
senses.whyCN: 从技能转到物件发生在 18 世纪，当时作品开始被作为艺术品收藏。

senses.title: Skill shown in doing
senses.definition: the visible skill with which something is performed
senses.definitionCN: 做某事时显现出来的技巧
senses.example: There is art in the way she leaves a sentence unfinished.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一句话留白的做法里有技巧。
senses.why: even in the fine-art sense, the old meaning of skill survives as the quality of the execution.
senses.whyCN: 即使在美术义里，古老的「技能」义仍作为执行的质量留存。

senses.title: The humanities
senses.definition: the subjects studied for culture and interpretation rather than utility, in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为文化与解释而非实用而学的学科，用复数
senses.example: The faculty of arts lost two departments.
senses.exampleCN: 文学院少了两个系。
senses.why: the university kept the Latin division between the arts and the sciences, and the plural marks it.
senses.whyCN: 大学保留了拉丁语中人文与科学的分野，复数即其标记。

senses.title: Cunning
senses.definition: the older sense of crafty design or deceit
senses.definitionCN: 狡黠设计或欺瞒的旧义
senses.example: The old play calls flattery an art of the weak.
senses.exampleCN: 那出老戏把谄媚称作弱者的计谋。
senses.why: skill without a moral aim was called art in the sense of artifice, and that shade survives in artful.
senses.whyCN: 不带道德目标的技巧曾被称作 artifice 意义上的 art，这层色彩存于 artful。

senses.title: Visual material
senses.definition: the illustrations and images prepared for a publication or product
senses.definitionCN: 为出版物或产品准备的插图与图像
senses.example: The editor asked for the art before the captions.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑要求在配文之前先交图。
senses.why: the printing trade narrowed art to the images it handles, a specialist use of the mass noun.
senses.whyCN: 印刷行业把 art 收窄为它处理的图像，是这一不可数名词的专业用法。

senses.title: A performing discipline
senses.definition: one of the performing disciplines, such as dance, music or theatre
senses.definitionCN: 表演门类之一，如舞蹈、音乐或戏剧
senses.example: Each art has its own way of rehearsing.
senses.exampleCN: 每一种表演门类都有自己的排练方式。
senses.why: counting forms requires a countable use, and this supplies one for the stage arts.
senses.whyCN: 要数不同形式就需要可数用法，这一义项为舞台艺术提供。

intro.en: Art comes through Old French from Latin ars (stem art-), which meant 'skill, craft, method' before it meant fine art. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: art 经古法语来自拉丁 ars（词干 art-），在指美术之前意为「技艺、手艺、方法」。年代均为约数。
