items.en: Ars meant 'skill, craft, a trained method', covering rhetoric, medicine and farming as well as sculpture. Its deeper origin is not established; the link to a root meaning 'to fit together' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺、手艺、训练有素的方法」，既指修辞、医学与农耕，也指雕刻。其更深来源未得到证明；与「拼合」词根的联系只是假说。

items.en: Ars plus the verb facere 'to make' produced artifex, 'craftsman', literally a maker by skill.
items.cn: ars 加动词 facere「制作」构成 artifex「匠人」，字面即凭技艺制作的人。

items.en: Old French art carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, still meaning learned skill or a method of doing.
items.cn: 古法语 art 在 13 世纪把这个词带入英语，当时仍指习得的技能或做事的办法。

items.en: Only in the eighteenth century did art settle into its modern sense of works valued for beauty, as collecting and academies separated art from craft.
items.cn: 直到 18 世纪，随着收藏与学院把美术与手艺分开，art 才落定为现代义：因美而受重视的作品。

items.en: The plural arts kept the older university sense of the liberal disciplines, as distinct from law, medicine and theology.
items.cn: 复数 arts 保留了较早的大学义，即与法律、医学、神学相对的博雅学科。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of ars is unsettled, and the widely repeated Indo-European root for 'fitting together' is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated ancestor.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ars 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论；常被引用的「拼合」印欧词根属重构形式，而非已证的祖先。

note.en: Group one shares the art or ars stem; group two holds words for skill and for creative work.
note.cn: 第一组共享 art 或 ars 词干；第二组是关于技艺与创作活动的词。

entries.definition: One who makes art, formed with -ist; the word art itself names the field or the works.
entries.definitionCN: 创作艺术的人，由 -ist 构成；art 本身指领域或作品。

entries.definition: Of art or of an artist's skill; it cannot replace art as the name of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 指艺术或艺术家技巧的；不能替代 art 作为领域名称。

entries.definition: Full of art in the old sense of craft, often with a hint of cunning, close to the sixth sense of art.
entries.definitionCN: 充满旧义「手艺」，常带狡黠之意，接近 art 的第六义。

entries.definition: Ars plus facere: a thing made by human skill, whether a tool or a relic, not necessarily a work of art.
entries.definitionCN: ars 加 facere：凭人力造出的物件，无论是工具还是遗物，不必是艺术品。

entries.definition: Making by trained hand, usually useful objects; art in the modern sense claims value beyond use.
entries.definitionCN: 以熟练的手工制作，通常是实用物件；现代义的艺术则主张超出用途的价值。

entries.definition: The plain word for trained ability, with no aesthetic claim; art as skill is its formal older cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 训练所得能力的平实说法，不含美学主张；作为技艺的 art 是它正式的旧表亲。

entries.definition: The planned arrangement of a made thing; art stresses expression, design stresses intention and function.
entries.definitionCN: 对制成之物的规划安排；art 强调表达，design 强调意图与功能。

entries.definition: The disciplines devoted to interpretation and culture; the plural arts is the British-leaning name for the same set.
entries.definitionCN: 致力于解释与文化的学科；复数 arts 是同一组学科偏英式的名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin ars 'skill': art began as knowing how, and only later became knowing what to look at.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ars「技艺」：艺术先是知道怎么做，后来才成为知道看什么。

normal.en: The family runs artist, artistic, artful, artless, artifact, artifice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 artist、artistic、artful、artless、artifact、artifice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: modern art, the art of conversation, a work of art, fine arts.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出义项：现代艺术、交谈的艺术、一件作品、美术。

normal.en: The plural changes the meaning: arts are the humanities, not several paintings.
normal.cn: 复数改变词义：arts 指人文学科，而非几幅画。

normal.en: Compare craft and art: one makes useful things well, the other makes things worth looking at.
normal.cn: 比较 craft 与 art：一个把有用的东西做好，一个做出值得看的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that knows exactly how much pressure a brush needs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手，精确知道笔需要多大压力。

abstract.en: Picture a room where a made object outlives the reason it was made.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，一件制成品比它被造的理由活得更久。

abstract.en: Picture a lie told so well that it is admired before it is condemned.
abstract.cn: 想象一个谎说得太好，在被谴责之前先被欣赏。

examples.en: She studied art in a city that had lost its academy.
examples.cn: 她在一座失去学院的城里学艺术。

examples.en: The art of the deal lay in saying less.
examples.cn: 这笔交易的艺术在于少说话。

examples.en: The museum keeps the art in a basement with a steady temperature.
examples.cn: 博物馆把作品存放在温度稳定的地下室里。

dict_mnemonic.text: art＝「会做」：先会做一件事，再做出值得看的东西；记「技艺 → 作品 → 学科」。

root: 拉丁 ars（词干 art-）「技艺、手艺、方法」，其更深来源不确定，常被引用的「拼合」词根属重构形式；经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow skill outward: the field, a practised ability, works made to be seen, the skill visible in execution, the humanities, cunning, pictures for print, and one performing discipline among several.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从技艺向外展开：门类、熟练本领、供观看的作品、执行中可见的技巧、人文学科、狡诈、印刷用图，以及若干表演门类中的一门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that knows the pressure a brush needs, and a painting that outlives the reason for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只知道笔下力道的收，以及一幅比其制作理由活得更久的画。

branches.en: FIELD AND ABILITY: the whole activity, then the trained how-to inside it.
branches.cn: 领域与能力：整片活动，以及其中的熟练方法。

branches.en: OBJECT AND EXECUTION: the thing hung on a wall, and the skill visible in how it was made.
branches.cn: 物件与执行：挂在墙上的东西，以及制作方式中可见的技巧。

branches.en: THE CAMPUS SENSE: arts as the disciplines of interpretation.
branches.cn: 校园义：arts 作为解释的学科。

branches.en: THE SHADOW: skill detached from a good aim becomes cunning.
branches.cn: 阴影：脱离正当目标的技巧变成狡诈。

branches.en: NARROW USES: pictures for a page, and one discipline among the performing arts.
branches.cn: 窄用：页面上的图，以及表演艺术中的一门。

intro.en: Art is a Latin noun with almost no affix of its own, but its stem and its relatives carry the whole family of skill words.
intro.cn: art 是一个几乎没有自带词缀的拉丁名词，但其词干与亲属承载了整个「技艺」词族。

latinIntro.en: Ars gives art, artist, artistic, artifact and artifice; the plural arts gives the liberal disciplines.
latinIntro.cn: ars 衍生 art、artist、artistic、artifact、artifice；复数 arts 给出博雅学科。

items.example: Ars covered rhetoric before it covered painting.
items.exampleCN: ars 先指修辞，后指绘画。

items.example: The artifex works by trained hand.
items.exampleCN: 匠人凭训练过的手工作。

items.example: Art first meant knowing how.
items.exampleCN: art 起初指知道怎么做。

items.example: The artist ground her own pigment.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家自己研磨颜料。

items.example: The artistic decision came before the budget.
items.exampleCN: 艺术上的决定先于预算。

items.example: An artful pause changed the verdict.
items.exampleCN: 一次巧妙的停顿改变了裁定。

items.example: Her artless question got a true answer.
items.exampleCN: 她天真的提问得到了真话。

items.meaning: an object made by human skill
items.example: Every artifact in the trench was catalogued.
items.exampleCN: 壕沟里的每件人工制品都被登记。

items.example: The artifice was visible only afterwards.
items.exampleCN: 那套巧技事后才看得出来。
